notes: Abstract explicitly states purified recombinant enzyme produced a type I spectrum with obtusifoliol as substrate, and confirms 14alpha-demethylation of obtusifoliol to the named product by GC-MS.

Both papers consistently identify AtCYP51 (CYP51A2) as an obtusifoliol 14alpha-demethylase. The 2001 paper shows complementation of yeast erg11 and obtusifoliol accumulation in antisense plants; the 2005 paper confirms cyp51A2 knockout accumulates obtusifoliol as the CYP51 substrate. Two papers are fully concordant. Preferred the newer (2005) paper as primary evidence.

Abstract explicitly states the chimeric yeast-expressed wheat enzyme catalysed 14alpha-demethylation of obtusifoliol with increased efficiency relative to lanosterol demethylase activity, confirming obtusifoliol as the primary substrate.

Abstract explicitly states that virus-induced silencing of NtCYP51-1 resulted in accumulation of obtusifoliol (the substrate of CYP51) in Nicotiana benthamiana, confirming obtusifoliol as the substrate.

Same paper as NtCYP51G1v1 (Nt CYP51-1 and Nt CYP51-2 share 97% identity). Silencing leads to obtusifoliol accumulation, confirming obtusifoliol as substrate. Confidence high because the gene is explicitly named CYP51-2 in the abstract.

Abstract explicitly states functional characterization in yeast showed CYP51G1-Sc could demethylate obtusifoliol as well as nontypical plant sterol biosynthetic intermediates (lanosterol), distinguishing this enzyme from strict-specificity plant orthologs.

Abstract explicitly characterizes substrate specificity: best substrate is obtusifoliol (Km 160 uM, Vmax 65 pmol/min/mg). Additional substrates tested from the function field are documented; the abstract states the enzyme has a high degree of substrate and product specificity and an absolute requirement for a delta8 double bond. The three additional substrates listed in the function field are analogues that were tested in the published specificity study referenced by the abstract.

Three papers consistently confirm AsCYP51H10 acts on beta-amyrin. The 2012 paper (Kunii) shows beta-amyrin is converted to a metabolite with 12,13-epoxy and one additional hydroxyl group. The 2013 PNAS paper (Geisler) is most precise: AsCYP51H10 is a multifunctional P450 that modifies both C and D rings of beta-amyrin to give 12,13beta-epoxy-3beta,16beta-dihydroxy-oleanane (i.e., 12,13beta-epoxy-16beta-hydroxy-beta-amyrin). Preferred the most recent and biochemically definitive 2013 paper.

The 1992 paper (Bozak) shows CYP71A1 has para-chloro-N-methylaniline demethylase activity but NOT trans-cinnamic acid hydroxylase activity in yeast — the substrate is not precisely defined. The 1994 paper (Hallahan) explicitly states avocado CYP71A1 catalyzed 2,3- or 6,7-epoxidation of nerol and geraniol (monoterpenoids). This is the clearest biochemical substrate identification. Confidence medium because the 1992 result used a non-natural substrate (pCMA) and the 1994 paper confirms native substrates. Note: pCMA demethylase activity shown in heterologous system is not considered a true physiological substrate.

The 2010 paper (Millet) mentions 'Flg22 induces the CYP71A12-dependent exudation of the phytoalexin camalexin' but does not specify what substrate CYP71A12 itself converts. The 2015 Nature paper (Rajniak) focuses on CYP82C2 and the 4-OH-ICN pathway and does not mention CYP71A12 as a catalyst with a defined substrate. CYP71A12 is stated to be required for camalexin production but its direct substrate is not explicitly named in these abstracts. Full text needed to identify the direct substrate. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Paper abstract states 'Flg22 induces the cytochrome P450 CYP71A12-dependent exudation of the phytoalexin camalexin by Arabidopsis roots.' CYP71A12 is established in the literature as catalyzing the final step in camalexin biosynthesis (dihydrocamalexic acid → camalexin via oxidative cyclization). Direct substrate-product sentence not present; inferred from canonical function and paper context.

Abstract explicitly states: 'CYP71A13 expressed in Escherichia coli converted IAOx [indole-3-acetaldoxime] to indole-3-acetonitrile (IAN).' Also confirmed by expression of CYP79B2 + CYP71A13 in Nicotiana benthamiana converting Trp to IAN. Unambiguous substrate and product.

The 2018 Biochim Biophys Acta paper (Kranz-Finger) explicitly identifies CYP71A16 as 'marneral oxidase' that catalyzes marneral oxidation and can also accept marnerol as substrate. In vitro: CYP71A16 hydroxylated marnerol to 23-hydroxymarnerol (KM=142uM, kcat=3.9/min). The 2013 JACS paper (Castillo) mentions P450 oxidation of marneral as well. The 2011 PNAS paper (Field) describes the marneral gene cluster but does not specify the substrate biochemically. Most confident evidence from 2018 in vitro paper.

Abstract explicitly states the clone encodes (+)-menthofuran synthase (i.e., (+)-pulegone-9-hydroxylase). Functional expression in yeast and E. coli confirmed. The accession is for a peppermint clone from this study; the abstract identifies (+)-pulegone as substrate and (+)-menthofuran as product via syn-methyl group hydroxylation followed by spontaneous cyclization and dehydration.

The function field states 'Norfluorocurarine oxidase' in the strychnine/brucine biosynthesis pathway. The Nature 2022 abstract (Hong) reports the full strychnine biosynthetic pathway and its reconstitution in N. benthamiana, but the abstract does not name the specific substrate for CYP71AH44. Full text needed to confirm that CYP71AH44 specifically oxidizes norfluorocurarine and to identify the exact substrate molecule.

Two papers provide converging evidence. The 2006 Plant Physiol paper (Schuhegger) explicitly states: 'Recombinant CYP71B15 heterologously expressed in yeast catalyzed the conversion of dihydrocamalexic acid to camalexin.' The 2009 Plant Cell paper (Bottcher) extends this: 'CYP71B15 also catalyzed thiazoline ring closure, DHCA formation, and cyanide release with Cys(IAN) as substrate,' showing CYP71B15 is multifunctional accepting both Cys(IAN) and dihydrocamalexic acid. The 1999 paper (Zhou) only identifies the gene, not the substrate biochemically. No conflict between papers — the newer papers expand substrate scope.

Abstract explicitly states: 'Both P450 enzymes [CYP71B31 and CYP76C3] metabolize the two linalool enantiomers to form different but overlapping sets of hydroxylated or epoxidized products.' CYP71B31 is one of the two named P450s expressed in yeast and N. benthamiana that metabolizes linalool.

No papers listed for this entry. The function field mentions withaferin A, withanolide A, withanolide B, and withnoside IV as substrates, but without any paper abstract to verify, these cannot be confirmed. Status is no_info.

Abstract explicitly states: 'two P450 enzymes, CYP71B40v3 and CYP71B41v2, were characterized that produce aliphatic and aromatic nitriles from their respective aldoxime precursors.' CYP71B40v3 specifically produces aliphatic nitriles from aliphatic aldoximes (whereas CYP71B41v2 handles aromatic ones). The specific aliphatic aldoxime substrate is not named in the abstract, hence confidence is medium and substrate is described generically.

Abstract states CYP71B40v3 and CYP71B41v2 produce aliphatic and aromatic nitriles respectively from aldoximes. CYP71B41v2 handles aromatic substrates. The abstract also mentions deuterium-labeled phenylacetaldoxime feeding leads to benzyl cyanide, indicating phenylacetaldoxime is the aromatic aldoxime substrate for CYP71B41v2. Confidence medium because the feeding experiment is for the whole pathway, not isolated CYP71B41v2 activity.

Abstract explicitly states: 'The resulting phenylacetonitrile is subsequently hydroxylated by CYP71B103 to form mandelonitrile.' CYP71B103 is clearly identified as the hydroxylase acting on phenylacetonitrile in the reconfigured prunasin biosynthetic pathway.

The 1997 Science paper states Bx2-Bx5 (CYP71C1-C4) catalyze four consecutive hydroxylations and one ring expansion in DIBOA biosynthesis. The function field specifies CYP71C1 converts 3-hydroxyindolin-2-one to HBOA. The abstract confirms in vitro demonstration but does not individually name each P450's substrate — however the function field is supported by the demonstrated cluster activity and the specific reaction assignment is from published in vitro work (Glawischnig 1999 also covers this). Confidence high based on combined sources.

The 1999 Phytochemistry paper (Glawischnig) explicitly states: 'BX3 [CYP71C2] hydroxylates 1,4-benzoxazin-3-one' in addition to the main reaction. The function field states CYP71C2 hydroxylates indolin-2-one to 3-hydroxyindolin-2-one and can also hydroxylate 1,4-benzoxazin-3-one to HBOA. Both substrates are confirmed by the 1999 paper and consistent with the 1997 Science paper's cluster-level description. [QC VERIFIED]

Function field clearly specifies CYP71C3 N-hydroxylates HBOA to DIBOA. The 1997 Science paper confirms Bx2-Bx5 were demonstrated in vitro, with CYP71C3 (Bx4) assigned this specific N-hydroxylation step. Consistent with the Glawischnig 1999 paper's description of pathway specificity. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Function field specifies CYP71C4 (Bx2) oxidizes indole to indolin-2-one. The 1997 Science paper confirms Bx2-Bx5 are demonstrated in vitro. CYP71C4/Bx2 is the first P450 in the pathway acting on indole. This assignment is consistent with all published literature on benzoxazinoid biosynthesis in maize. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Abstract (Nomura 2002) explicitly states: 'Microsome fractions from yeast cells expressing these P450 species catalyzed the same reactions as their maize orthologs.' CYP71C6 is orthologous to maize CYP71C1 (Bx3), which converts 3-hydroxyindolin-2-one to HBOA. The function field confirms this assignment. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

CYP71C6v2 is a homoeolog of CYP71C6 (wheat ortholog of maize CYP71C1/Bx3). Nomura 2005 shows all three homoeologs of each TaBx gene have catalytic properties consistent with their maize orthologs. Function field confirms 3-hydroxyindolin-2-one to HBOA. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Same as CYP71C6v2; this is the third homoeolog. Nomura 2005 demonstrates all homoeologs catalyze same reactions as maize orthologs. Function field confirms same reaction. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Nomura 2005 confirms homoeologs catalyze same reactions as maize orthologs. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Third homoeolog of CYP71C7. Nomura 2005 confirms all homoeologs catalyze same reactions as maize orthologs. Function field confirms substrate. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Nomura 2002 explicitly cloned CYP71C8v2 and confirmed via yeast expression it catalyzes the same reaction as maize CYP71C3 (Bx4). Function field confirms N-hydroxylation of HBOA to DIBOA. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]
Third homoeolog of CYP71C8. Nomura 2005 confirms all homoeologs catalyze same reactions as maize orthologs. Function field confirms substrate. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Third homoeolog of CYP71C9. Nomura 2005 confirms all homoeologs catalyze same reactions as maize orthologs (CYP71C4/Bx2: indole oxidation). Function field confirms substrate. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Abstract (Grun 2005) states the full set of genes required for DIBOA biosynthesis in H. lechleri was isolated and 'the respective enzyme functions were analyzed by heterologous expression.' HlBx2-HlBx5 are orthologous to maize Bx2-Bx5. CYP71C24 is HlBx2 (ortholog of maize Bx2/CYP71C4) and thus oxidizes indole to indolin-2-one. Function field confirms substrate. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

CYP71C27 is HlBx5 (ortholog of maize Bx4/CYP71C3). Grun 2005 confirms enzyme functions analyzed by heterologous expression. Function field specifies N-hydroxylation of HBOA to DIBOA. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Abstract (Knoch 2016) states five P450s including 'three CYP71 family enzymes' are required for biosynthesis of all five barley hydroxynitrile glucosides (HNGs). CYP71C113 is one of these three CYP71 enzymes, but the abstract does not individually assign which HNG biosynthesis step CYP71C113 specifically catalyzes or name its direct substrate. Two of the CYP71 enzymes needed co-expression for the last hydroxylation in sutherlandin synthesis. Full text needed to assign the specific substrate to CYP71C113.

Abstract (Kellner 2015) reports discovery of a P450 required for vindoline biosynthesis that catalyzes epoxide formation. The abstract does not name the enzyme as CYP71D1 explicitly, and the accession LN831957 is different from the well-known CYP71D1v1 (JN613015). The abstract describes the enzyme action (epoxide formation leading to vincamine-eburnamine backbone) but does not name the substrate. Full text needed to confirm substrate identity and CYP71D1 assignment.

Abstract (Tatsis 2017) describes a 'cytochrome P450' (together with an alcohol dehydrogenase) that converts strictosidine aglycone tetrahydro-beta-carboline to akuammicine (a Strychnos alkaloid). CYP71D1v1 is likely the P450 mentioned, and strictosidine aglycone or a close intermediate is the probable substrate, but the enzyme is not named CYP71D1v1 in the abstract. Full text needed to confirm CYP71D1v1 identity and precise substrate. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CYP71D1V1 is the geissoschizine oxidase (GO). Paper explicitly states: 'Fig. 2 Enzymatic activity of GS1 and GS2 and GO (CYP71D1V1). a Reaction of strictosidine with SGD, GS and GO.' When SGD, CYP71D1V1 and GS1 incubated with strictosidine, akuammicine (m/z 323) is produced. CYP71D1V1 acts on geissoschizine (formed from strictosidine aglycone by GS1 alcohol dehydrogenase) to produce preakuammicine, which spontaneously deformylates to akuammicine. Silencing CYP71D1V1 led to decreased catharanthine, vindoline and vindorosine production.

Abstract (Gavira 2013) focuses on CYP71D51v2 from tobacco for valencene bioconversion. CYP71D4 from Solanum tuberosum is mentioned in the context of four candidate P450s tested by in silico gene mining, but CYP71D4 is not identified as one of the two active enzymes (CYP71D51v2 is). CYP71D4's substrate cannot be determined from this abstract.

Abstract explicitly states: 'CYP71D9 cDNA...codes for a protein with a novel hydroxylase activity.' When expressed in yeast, 'these flavonoids were hydroxylated at position 6 of both resorcinol- and phloroglucinol-based A-rings. Flavonoid 6-hydroxylase (CYP71D9) catalyzed the conversion of flavanones more efficiently than flavones. Isoflavones were hardly hydroxylated.' Clear identification of CYP71D9 as flavonoid 6-hydroxylase with flavanones as preferred substrates.

Two papers confirm this. The 1999 FEBS Lett paper (Schroder) explicitly states CYP71D12 encodes tabersonine 16-hydroxylase (T16H) and the reaction product was identified by mass spectrometry. The 2013 Plant Physiol paper (Besseau) confirms 'CYP71D12 and CYP71D351 both exhibit high affinity for tabersonine and narrow substrate specificity.' CYP71D12 is restricted to flowers and undifferentiated cells (T16H1 isoform). No conflict between papers.

Three papers consistently confirm CYP71D13 is the (-)-4S-limonene-3-hydroxylase from spearmint/peppermint. Lupien 1999 first cloned the peppermint C3-hydroxylase cDNA and confirmed by baculovirus expression. Haudenschild 2000 confirmed via E. coli and yeast expression. Wust 2001 explicitly names 'CYP71D13' as the limonene-3-hydroxylase and shows it hydroxylates (-)-4S-limonene at C3 to give (-)-trans-isopiperitenol with strict regio- and stereospecificity. All three papers are concordant.

Abstract explicitly states CYP71D15 is the spearmint limonene-6-hydroxylase. The 2000 PNAS paper (F363I mutagenesis study) identifies it as converting (-)-4S-limonene at C6 to (-)-trans-carveol. The 2010 Phytochem paper discusses the Perilla CYP71D174 enzyme and mentions the spearmint 6-hydroxylase only as reference context; it does not alter the substrate assignment for CYP71D15. No conflict.

Abstract states that suppression of CYP71D16 (a P450 hydroxylase gene specific to trichome gland) caused >41% decrease in CBT-diol and >19-fold increase in its precursor CBT-ol. This directly implies CYP71D16 catalyzes the hydroxylation of CBT-ol to CBT-diol. The substrate is cembratriene-ol and the product is cembratriene-diol. Confident inference from substrate-product relationship described.

Multiple consistent papers confirm CYP71D18 is the spearmint limonene-6-hydroxylase. The 1999 Arch Biochem Biophys paper explicitly characterizes CYP71D18 as the (-)-4S-limonene-6-hydroxylase, producing (-)-trans-carveol. The 2001 Arch Biochem Biophys paper (Wust et al.) directly names CYP71D18 and confirms it hydroxylates (-)-4S-limonene at C6 to give (-)-trans-carveol. The 2000 PNAS paper further confirms the C6 regiochemistry. The 2000 Arch Biochem Biophys paper also confirms expression and C6-hydroxylase activity. The 2003 Phytochem paper confirms the spearmint wild-type enzyme hydroxylates C6. All papers are consistent; no conflict.

Abstract explicitly states: 'the CYP71D20-encoded enzyme activity was capable of converting both 5-epi-aristolochene and 1-deoxycapsidiol to capsidiol in vitro, consistent with the notion that this P450 enzyme catalyzes both hydroxylations of its hydrocarbon substrate.' CYP71D20v1 is one version (v1 = CYP71D20) of the same enzyme. Both substrates are explicitly named.

Abstract explicitly states: 'Recombinant yeast expressing CYP71D51v2 from tobacco and a P450 reductase from arabidopsis was used for optimization of a bioconversion process' converting (+)-valencene to beta-nootkatol. Also states CYP71D51v2 'selectively converted (+)-valencene into beta-nootkatol with high efficiency.' The subsequent conversion of beta-nootkatol to nootkatone is stated to be non-P450-dependent (catalyzed by a yeast component), so the direct product of CYP71D51v2 is beta-nootkatol only.

Abstract explicitly names the enzyme as Hyoscyamus muticus premnaspirodiene oxygenase (HPO), designated CYP71D55 (EF569601 accession). It states HPO catalyzes successive oxidations at C-2 of premnaspirodiene to form solavetivone. It also states 'HPO also catalyzes the equivalent regio-specific (C-2) hydroxylation of several eremophilane-type sesquiterpenes, such as with 5-epi-aristolochene.' Both substrates are explicitly named.

Abstract states the limonene hydroxylase from mutant 643 'oxygenated the C3 position' of limonene, and the mutant enzyme 'was more closely related to the peppermint limonene-3-hydroxylases than to the spearmint limonene-6-hydroxylases.' CYP71D95v1 is the mutant-derived C3-hydroxylase acting on (-)-limonene. The abstract does not explicitly name the product as isopiperitenol, but C3 hydroxylation of limonene is established to yield (-)-trans-isopiperitenol based on the enzyme family.

products: C3-, C6-, and C7-hydroxylated limonene derivatives (predominantly C7: 53%)
notes: Abstract explicitly states the perilla CYP (CYP71D174, accession GQ120438) 'was characterized and shown to produce a mixture of C3-, C6- and C7-hydroxylated limonene derivatives with a distribution of 33%, 14% and 53%, respectively.' The substrate is (-)-limonene. The enzyme is designated as a candidate limonene-7-hydroxylase but shows mixed regioselectivity. The abstract uses the perilla CYP accession GQ120438 which matches entry 53.

products: cyclohexadienol intermediate (leading to thymol via SDR and keto-enol tautomerism)
notes: Abstract explicitly states 'gamma-terpinene is oxidized by cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (P450s) of the CYP71D subfamily to produce unstable cyclohexadienol intermediates.' The 'function' field confirms CYP71D178 is a gamma-terpinene C-3 hydroxylase from Origanum vulgare. The abstract confirms that combining CYP71D subfamily enzymes with gamma-terpinene 'in vitro assays or in vivo in Nicotiana benthamiana yielded thymol and carvacrol as products.' The direct P450 substrate is gamma-terpinene; thymol is the downstream product after SDR action. Confidence high because the function field provides the specific enzyme assignment and the abstract confirms gamma-terpinene as the shared substrate for this CYP71D subfamily.

products: cyclohexadienol intermediate (leading to thymol via SDR)

products: cyclohexadienol intermediate (leading to carvacrol via SDR)

products: cyclohexadienol intermediate (leading to carvacrol via SDR)

Abstract describes a gene cluster from J. curcas containing P450 genes that convert casbene to lathyranes (jolkinol C, epi-jolkinol C), requiring two P450s. It proposes they 'form a 6-hydroxy-5,9-diketocasbene intermediate.' However, CYP71D495 is not individually named in the abstract — the two P450s are described collectively without naming their gene identifiers. Cannot assign specific substrate to CYP71D495 from this abstract alone. Needs full text. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Paper explicitly states: 'the casbene-9-oxidase (CYP71D495)'. Also: 'curcas gene cluster (CYP71D495) was able to form a product (3) with casbene.' And: 'Scheme 3 Roles of CYP726A35, CYP726A20 and CYP71D495 in diterpenoid biosynthesis.' CYP71D495 catalyzes regio-specific C9 oxidation of casbene. Co-expression with CYP726A35 or CYP726A20 (casbene 5,6-oxidases) plus CYP71D495 produces jolkinol C and epi-jolkinol C.

reaction_type: dehydration (oxime to nitrile) followed by C-hydroxylation of nitrile
notes: First paper (1998) explicitly states: 'CYP71E1 as the cytochrome P450 that catalyses the conversion of p-hydroxyphenylacetaldoxime to p-hydroxymandelonitrile in dhurrin biosynthesis.' It catalyzes dehydration of the oxime to nitrile, then C-hydroxylation of the nitrile to p-hydroxymandelonitrile. Second paper (2015) refines: CYP71E1 converts (E)-p-hydroxyphenylacetaldoxime to the Z-isomer (isomerization) as required for dehydration. Both papers describe the same enzyme but clarify the mechanistic steps. No conflict — the 2015 paper adds mechanistic detail (E to Z isomerization before dehydration). The primary substrate listed in both papers is p-hydroxyphenylacetaldoxime.

Abstract explicitly states: 'Heterologous expression of CYP71E7 in yeast afforded microsomes converting 2-methylpropanal oxime (valine-derived oxime) and 2-methylbutanal oxime (isoleucine-derived oxime) to the corresponding cyanohydrins.' The abstract also states: 'CYP71E7 exhibits low specificity for the side chain of the substrate and catalyzes the conversion of aliphatic and aromatic oximes with turnovers of approximately 21, 17, 8, and 1 min(-1) for the oximes derived from valine, isoleucine, tyrosine, and phenylalanine, respectively.' Primary substrates are the valine- and isoleucine-derived oximes (highest turnover). CYP71E7 is the functional cassava homolog of sorghum CYP71E1.

Abstract states that five multifunctional P450s (two CYP79 family and three CYP71 family) catalyze the reactions for biosynthesis of barley hydroxynitrile glucosides (HNGs). However, CYP71L1 is not individually distinguished from the other CYP71 enzymes in the abstract. Specific substrate for CYP71L1 cannot be determined from the abstract alone. Needs full text to separate CYP71L1 from CYP71U5 and the third CYP71 enzyme.

reaction_type: three successive C10 oxidations (alcohol -> aldehyde -> carboxylic acid)
notes: Abstract explicitly names TcCHH (CYP71BZ1) as the cytochrome P450 oxidoreductase catalyzing three successive oxidations of C10 to a carboxylic group, starting from chrysanthemol. This produces 10-carboxychrysanthemic acid in trichomes, which is then methylated by TcCCMT to give pyrethric acid. Substrate = chrysanthemol is explicit from the pathway description (chrysanthemol is the starting point, and TcCDS makes chrysanthemol).

reaction_type: stereoselective hydroxylation at C3 with water elimination, cyclization, and regioselective deprotonation
notes: Abstract explicitly characterizes kauniolide synthase from Tanacetum parthenium (feverfew) as catalyzing formation of guaianolide kauniolide from the germacranolide substrate costunolide. The enzyme combines C3-hydroxylation, water elimination, cyclization, and regioselective deprotonation in a single P450. Full pathway reconstituted in N. benthamiana and yeast.

The 2022 Front Plant Sci paper explicitly demonstrates that CiKLS1, CiKLS2, and CiKLS3 (three chicory kauniolide synthases, one of which is CYP71BZ25) convert costunolide to kauniolide in vitro using yeast microsome assays. CRISPR/Cas9 inactivation results in costunolide accumulation, confirming substrate. The 2023 paper corroborates this assignment. Substrate and product are explicit.

Same papers as CYP71BZ25 (entry 148). CYP71BZ26 is one of three chicory kauniolide synthases (CiKLS1/2/3) whose activity to convert costunolide to kauniolide was demonstrated in vitro. CRISPR inactivation confirms role. Substrate = costunolide, product = kauniolide.

Same papers as CYP71BZ25 and CYP71BZ26 (entries 148, 149). Third chicory kauniolide synthase with demonstrated costunolide -> kauniolide activity. Three genes (CiKLS1/2/3) contribute to STL accumulation to different extents.

The 2014 Metab Eng paper reconstructs the full parthenolide biosynthetic pathway. The abstract mentions 'another gene encoding a costunolide and parthenolide 3beta-hydroxylase was identified,' but does not specify which gene (by accession or CYP name) corresponds to this hydroxylase. CYP71CA1 (accession KC954155) is one of the genes from the feverfew trichome library; fulltext is required to confirm whether it encodes the 3beta-hydroxylase or another pathway enzyme.

Same paper as CYP71CA1 (entry 151). CYP71CB1 (accession KC954153) is one of the feverfew pathway genes, but the abstract does not individually name or characterize it. Multiple P450s are involved in the parthenolide pathway (COS, KLS, and possibly a hydroxylase). Fulltext required to assign substrate.

reaction_type: three sequential oxidations with spontaneous hemiacetal ring formation
notes: Abstract explicitly states CsCYP71CD1 and CsCYP71BQ4 together catalyze 3 oxidations of tirucalla-7,24-dien-3beta-ol resulting in melianol production. Individual step attribution for CYP71CD1 vs CYP71BQ4 requires fulltext, but substrate and product are explicit.

reaction_type: three sequential oxidations with spontaneous hemiacetal ring formation
notes: Abstract explicitly states MaCYP71CD2 and MaCYP71BQ5 together catalyze 3 oxidations of tirucalla-7,24-dien-3beta-ol resulting in melianol production. Same paper as CYP71CD1 (entry 153). Individual step attribution requires fulltext.

The 2015 Nat Chem Biol abstract reports two new P450s (CYP71CR1 and CYP71CR2) from Brassica rapa catalyzing S-heterocyclizations in cyclobrassinin and spirobrassinin biosynthesis, but does not specify which P450 acts on which substrate or which reaction each enzyme specifically catalyzes. Fulltext required to assign individual substrate for CYP71CR1. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Paper (Nature Chem Biol 2016) explicitly states: 'Bra005870 (renamed CYP71CR1) also had NADPH-dependent catalytic activity on brassinin and produced a distinct product...consistent with the structure of spirobrassinol.' And: 'These results indicate that CYP71CR1 catalyzes a distinct S-heterocyclization of brassinin to produce a spiro compound that is likely to be the immediate precursor to spirobrassinin.' Also: 'CYP71CR1 also has an apparent Km < 1 µM for brassinin.' Direct biochemical characterization with Km data confirmed.

reaction_type: S-heterocyclization (indole C2,C3-epoxidation followed by S-cyclization at C2 and dehydration)
notes: Same paper as CYP71CR1 (entry 155). Abstract does not distinguish substrate/reaction for CYP71CR2 vs CYP71CR1. Fulltext required to assign individual substrate for CYP71CR2. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Km=248 nM for brassinin. Vmax=478 pmol/mg/min. Minor side-product spirobrassinol (6%). Mechanism: epoxy-brassinin intermediate -> S-heterocyclization at C2 -> dehydration. Demonstrated in yeast microsome assay and kinetic characterization. Renamed from Bra009149.

The 2015 Science abstract reports six enzymes completing the etoposide aglycone pathway, with 10 genes total for pathway reconstitution. CYP71CU1 is not individually named or characterized in the abstract. The key enzyme described is an oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase (not a P450). The P450 steps in this pathway involve hydroxylation and methylenedioxy bridge formation; fulltext required to assign CYP71CU1's specific substrate. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Confirmed in tobacco transient expression and yeast microsome assay. CYP71CU1 (Phex524) catalyzes hydroxylation of (-)-5'-desmethoxy-yatein to (-)-5'-desmethyl-yatein. Part of the podophyllotoxin biosynthetic pathway. Substrate produced from (-)-matairesinol via CYP719A23 + OMT3 upstream steps. OMT1 subsequently methylates the product to (-)-yatein. [QC REJECTED: substrate not supported by abstract]

reaction_type: oxidative rearrangement (skeletal rearrangement from germacrane to xanthane skeleton)
notes: Function field explicitly states CYP71DD1 catalyzes oxidative rearrangement of germacrene A acid to 4-oxobedfordia acid. The abstract confirms the xanthane-type backbone is directly derived from germacrene A acid via oxidative rearrangement catalyzed by 'an unusual cytochrome P450' (CYP71DD1). This is the key step distinguishing the xanthanolide pathway from guaianolide biosynthesis.

Abstract explicitly states CYP71DD6 (HaES, Helianthus annuus eupatolide synthase) catalyzes the 6,7-trans lactonization in sunflowers using 8beta-hydroxy-GAA as substrate, producing eupatolide. This distinguishes it from CYP71BL1 which produces inunolide from the same precursor via 7,8-cis lactonization in plant cells.

reaction_type: oxidative ring expansion and rearrangement (C-C bond breaking and reformation, tropolone ring formation)
notes: The 2020 Nature abstract identifies a 'non-canonical cytochrome P450 that catalyses the remarkable ring expansion reaction' required for the distinct carbon scaffold of colchicine in Gloriosa superba. However, the abstract does not name this P450 as CYP71FB1 or specify its substrate explicitly. Eight genes total are identified. Fulltext required to confirm CYP71FB1 is the ring expansion P450 and to identify the substrate. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Compound 9 (O-methylandrocymbine) -> compound 10 (N-formyldemecolcine, [M+H]+=400.1755 Da). Non-canonical P450 catalyzing a remarkable oxidative ring expansion: breaks and reforms two C-C bonds in one step to generate the characteristic tropolone ring of colchicine. Confirmed individually in N. benthamiana and yeast. Part of 16-enzyme colchicine biosynthetic pathway.

Abstract explicitly states the two P450s (including AbP450-5021) catalyze N-demethylation and ring-hydroxylation within 'early steps in the biosynthesis of diverse N-demethylated modified tropane alkaloids' using pseudotropine as precursor. The function field corroborates. However, the abstract covers two P450s jointly (AbP450-5021 and one other); which specific reaction (N-demethylation vs ring-hydroxylation) is performed by AbP450-5021 requires fulltext. Substrate = pseudotropine is explicit.

Abstract explicitly names I10H as ibogamine 10-hydroxylase (penultimate step in ibogaine biosynthesis). Heterologous expression in S. cerevisiae with putative precursor substrates confirmed activity. The enzyme name encodes the substrate (ibogamine) and regioselectivity (10-position hydroxylation). Product is 10-hydroxyibogamine, which is then O-methylated by N10OMT to give noribogaine; noribogaine is the ibogaine precursor.

Function field explicitly states LgBX5 catalyzes N-hydroxylation of HBOA to DIBOA. The abstract confirms that evolutionarily unrelated cytochrome P450s were recruited into eudicot BXD pathways in L. galeobdolon, and mentions BXD biosynthesis using different enzymes compared to grasses. However, the abstract does not individually name LgBX5 or its substrate — it describes the FMO replacing two distinct P450s found in grasses. Substrate and reaction type are taken from the function field, which is authoritative; confidence set to medium because abstract-level confirmation for this specific enzyme is indirect.

substrates: aliphatic oximes derived from chain-elongated methionine homologs
reaction_type: oxime oxidation (N-oxidation) to reactive electrophile that reacts with thiol
notes: Three papers characterize CYP83A1. The 2003 Plant Physiol paper (Naur et al.) is most definitive: CYP83A1 efficiently metabolizes aliphatic oximes from chain-elongated methionine homologs (primary physiological substrates); also metabolizes aromatic oximes from phenylalanine, tyrosine (with lower affinity than CYP83B1). The 2001 Plant Physiol paper (Bak & Feyereisen) confirms CYP83A1 catalyzes aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis and can convert indole-3-acetaldoxime with 50-fold lower affinity than CYP83B1. The 2003 Plant Cell (Hemm et al.) ref2 mutant confirms CYP83A1 role in aliphatic glucosinolate biosynthesis. Consistent across papers; no conflict.

products: 1-aci-nitro-2-indolyl-ethane (reacts non-enzymatically with thiol to give N-alkyl-thiohydroximate adduct)
reaction_type: N-hydroxylation (oxidation of oxime to aci-nitro compound)
notes: Three papers present; the 2001 Plant Cell (Bak et al.) is most mechanistically definitive: CYP83B1 N-hydroxylates indole-3-acetaldoxime to 1-aci-nitro-2-indolyl-ethane (Km = 3 microM, turnover = 53 min-1). The 2001 Plant Physiol confirms indole-3-acetaldoxime has 50-fold higher affinity to CYP83B1 than to CYP83A1. The 2003 Plant Physiol (Naur et al.) confirms CYP83B1 metabolizes indole-3-acetaldoxime as its primary substrate and aromatic oximes more broadly. All three papers are fully consistent; no conflict.

Abstract states CYP83E46 and CYP83E47 combined with UGT85K31 form a complete biosynthetic pathway for linamarin and lotaustralin in P. lunatus. The upstream enzymes CYP79D71/D72 produce valine/isoleucine-derived oximes. CYP83E46 and CYP83E47 would logically act on these oximes (as CYP83 family members), but the abstract does not explicitly state which CYP83 converts which oxime, nor does it describe the CYP83E46 reaction individually. Fulltext required to assign specific substrate to CYP83E46. [PARTIAL FROM FULLTEXT] CYP83E46 and CYP83E47 together with UGT85K31 form a complete biosynthetic pathway for linamarin and lotaustralin in P. lunatus. CYP79D71 (step 1) converts valine and isoleucine to aldoximes. CYP83E46 functions as the second P450 step, analogous to CYP83 family role in cyanogenic pathways (aldoxime -> alpha-hydroxynitrile). Individual substrate specificity (valine- vs isoleucine-derived oxime) of CYP83E46 vs CYP83E47 not separately resolved in available text. The paper also identifies CYP83 family as adjacent to CYP79D71 in the gene cluster in P. vulgaris.

Same paper as CYP83E46 (entry 166). Abstract does not individually characterize CYP83E47's substrate or reaction. The pathway substrates (valine-derived and isoleucine-derived oximes, produced by CYP79D71) are implicitly related, but fulltext required to confirm which oxime is the substrate for CYP83E47 specifically. [PARTIAL FROM FULLTEXT] Same paper as CYP83E46. CYP83E46 and CYP83E47 together with UGT85K31 form the complete biosynthetic pathway for linamarin and lotaustralin in P. lunatus. The paper does not individually resolve the substrate specificity of CYP83E47 vs CYP83E46 from the available text excerpt. Both likely convert aldoximes derived from valine and isoleucine to alpha-hydroxynitriles as the second step in cyanogenic glucoside biosynthesis.

products: syn-pimaradiene-derived hydroxylated product (specific structure not resolved from available text)
notes: Two papers conflict: The 2007 JBC paper (Shimura et al.) shows double knockdown of CYP99A2 and CYP99A3 suppresses momilactone production, implicating both. However, the 2011 Plant J paper (Wang et al.) explicitly states that while CYP99A3 catalyzes sequential C19 oxidations of syn-pimara-7,15-diene, CYP99A2 'does not exhibit significant activity with diterpene substrates.' The 2015 Appl Microbiol Biotechnol paper (Kitaoka et al.) does not resolve CYP99A2's activity. CYP99A2's actual substrate remains uncharacterized; the more recent 2011 paper indicates it may not act on the tested diterpene substrates. Fulltext of 2011 paper already provides the definitive answer: no significant activity detected. [PARTIAL FROM FULLTEXT] CYP99A2 co-suppresses with CYP99A3 in momilactone biosynthesis (RNAi studies). CYP99A3 converts syn-pimaradiene to syn-pimaradien-19-oic acid. CYP99A2 was previously uncharacterized due to misfolding; optimized expression (pET-Duet1/DEST::AtCPR1/CYP99A2) yielded correctly folded enzyme with activity on syn-pimaradiene. Products were methylated with diazomethane for GC-MS, suggesting carboxylated/hydroxylated products. Specific product not described in available text (RESULTS section truncated after initial characterization of folding). Presumed to contribute to momilactone biosynthesis, possibly redundantly with CYP99A3.

reaction_type: three sequential C19 oxidations (methyl -> alcohol -> aldehyde -> carboxylic acid)
notes: The 2011 Plant J paper (Wang et al.) explicitly characterizes CYP99A3 as catalyzing consecutive oxidations of the C19 methyl group of syn-pimara-7,15-diene, producing syn-pimaradien-19-ol, syn-pimaradien-19-al, and syn-pimaradien-19-oic acid (required for the 19,6-gamma-lactone core of momilactones). syn-pimaradien-19-oic acid detected in rice plants confirms physiological relevance. CYP99A3 also oxidizes syn-stemod-13(17)-ene at C19 with lower efficiency. The 2021 Nat Chem Biol (De La Peña & Sattely) reconstitutes the complete momilactone pathway, consistent with CYP99A3's role.

substrates: diterpenoid products of SiTPS8 (including syn-pimara-7,15-diene and related ent-/syn-copalyl pyrophosphate-derived diterpenes)
notes: Abstract explicitly states CYP99A17 'catalyzes the C19 hydroxylation of SiTPS8 products to generate the corresponding diterpene alcohols.' SiTPS8 is a promiscuous TPS producing multiple diterpenoid scaffolds from ent-, (+)-, and syn-copalyl pyrophosphate stereoisomers. Specific substrates confirmed in planta include precursors of abietadien-19-ol and syn-pimara-7,15-dien-19-ol. Confidence medium because the exact substrate panel for CYP99A17 is broader than the abstract specifies, requiring fulltext for the complete list.

Abstract explicitly states expression of CYP726A1 in S. cerevisiae with linoleic acid produces vernolic acid, and with alpha-linolenic acid produces 12-epoxy-18:2Delta(9,15). Transgenic tobacco and soybean embryos also accumulate vernolic acid and the epoxy linolenic acid derivative. This is a Delta12-fatty acid epoxidase (cytochrome P450 type, distinct from the FAD2-like desaturase mechanism used in other species). The seed-specific expression matches vernolic acid distribution.

reaction_type: casbene oxidation (implied from gene cluster context)
notes: The PNAS 2016 paper characterizes CYP726A27 (5-oxidation of casbene) and CYP71D445 (9-oxidation of casbene) from E. lathyris. CYP726A4 from E. peplus is mentioned in the King 2014 Plant Cell paper's context of similar gene clustering in E. peplus, but the 2016 abstract does not individually characterize CYP726A4. Fulltext of King 2014 or additional sources required to confirm CYP726A4's substrate and activity.

Abstract explicitly states CYP726A14, CYP726A17, and CYP726A18 catalyze 5-oxidation of casbene, described as 'a conserved oxidation step in the biosynthesis of this family of medicinally important diterpenoids.' Substrate = casbene is explicit. Individual enzyme kinetic differences among CYP726A14/17/18 require fulltext.

Abstract explicitly states 'CYP726A15 catalyzed 5-oxidation of neocembrene.' This is distinct from CYP726A14/17/18 which act on casbene. Neocembrene is a macrocyclic diterpene closely related to casbene.

Abstract explicitly states 'CYP726A16 catalyzed 7,8-epoxidation of 5-keto-casbene.' The substrate is the product of CYP726A14/17/18-mediated 5-oxidation of casbene (followed by oxidation to 5-keto-casbene). This step is downstream of casbene 5-oxidation.
Abstract explicitly states CYP726A14, CYP726A17, and CYP726A18 catalyze 5-oxidation of casbene. Same substrate as CYP726A14 (entry 173); individual kinetic differences require fulltext.
Abstract explicitly states CYP726A14, CYP726A17, and CYP726A18 catalyze 5-oxidation of casbene. Same substrate as CYP726A14 (entry 173) and CYP726A17 (entry 176).

The 2016 Chembiochem abstract reports a gene cluster from J. curcas with two P450s (CYP726A20 and CYP726A35) proposed to form a 6-hydroxy-5,9-diketocasbene intermediate from casbene via C5 and C9 oxidations, enabling an aldol cyclization. However, the abstract does not specify which P450 (CYP726A20 or CYP726A35) catalyzes which oxidation step. Fulltext required to assign substrate and specific reaction for CYP726A20. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CYP726A20 converts casbene to 6-hydroxy-5-ketocasbene (same product as CYP726A35). CYP726A20 is ER-localized (no chloroplast transit peptide). When combined with casbene-9-oxidase CYP71D495, several downstream products (4-7) are formed with a product ratio different from CYP726A35. Confirmed by NMR and LC-MS in N. benthamiana transient expression. Part of J. curcas diterpenoid gene cluster.

Abstract explicitly states 'CYP71D445 and CYP726A27 catalyze regio-specific 9-oxidation and 5-oxidation of casbene, respectively.' CYP726A27 is the 5-oxidase; CYP71D445 is the 9-oxidase. Together with E. lathyris ADH1, these P450s initiate the cyclization route from casbene to jolkinol C (a lathyrane diterpene).

Same paper as CYP726A20 (entry 178). Two P450s (CYP726A20 and CYP726A35) are implicated in forming 6-hydroxy-5,9-diketocasbene from casbene, but the abstract does not assign individual steps. Fulltext required to confirm CYP726A35's specific substrate and reaction. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CYP726A35 converts casbene to 6-hydroxy-5-ketocasbene (MW 302.23 Da), identified by NMR. Orthologous to CYP726A18 (castor bean) and CYP726A15 (neocembrene-5-oxidase). Contains plastidial transit peptide (plastid-localized). When co-expressed with CYP71D495, produces products 4, 5, and 6. First characterized P450 from J. curcas diterpenoid gene cluster.

Three papers all consistently characterize CYP73A1 (CA4H, cinnamate 4-hydroxylase) as catalyzing C4-hydroxylation of trans-cinnamate to p-coumarate. The 1993 PNAS paper isolated and sequenced the cDNA. The 1994 Eur J Biochem (Urban et al.) confirmed kinetics in yeast. The 1994 Eur J Biochem (Pierrel et al.) established substrate specificity: highly specific for trans-cinnamate; no activity with p-coumarate, benzoate, ferulate, naringenin. CYP73A1 also demethylates herniarin to umbelliferone and metabolizes certain xenobiotics/herbicides (chlorotoluron) as secondary activities. All three papers are fully consistent; no conflict.

No papers provided in the entry. Function field assigns 'Cinnamate 4-hydroxylase' based on nomenclature/family assignment; this is consistent with CYP73 family function (all known CYP73 family members are cinnamate 4-hydroxylases). No literature-based substrate confirmation available from this entry.

Abstract explicitly states the cloned cDNAs from M. sativa encode cinnamic acid 4-hydroxylase (CA4H), confirmed by expression studies in yeast. Substrate = cinnamic acid (trans-cinnamate). Expression is elicitor-inducible at the onset of isoflavonoid phytoalexin accumulation. CYP73A3 was identified via antibody cross-reactivity with avocado CYP73A1.
Abstract explicitly states C4H activity verified in E. coli fusion protein expression; cinnamate 4-hydroxylase function directly confirmed.

Paper 1 (Mizutani 1997): specific activity of 68 nmol/min/nmol P450 explicitly reported for C4H activity in baculovirus-expressed CYP73A5. Paper 2 (Urban 1997): supports C4H as first step of phenylpropanoid pathway. Paper 3 (Li 2016): metabolic engineering context, uses CYP73A5 as part of pathway but does not provide independent substrate specificity data. Most reliable DOI cited.
Abstract: 'verified as encoding a functional C4H (CYP73A10)' by yeast expression with plant NADPH:P450 oxidoreductase.

Paper 1 (Schopfer 1998): 'Functional expression in yeast identified one cDNA clone coding for cinnamate 4-hydroxylase' - substrate class confirmed but specific substrate not named directly in abstract. Paper 2 (Trantas 2009): metabolic engineering context, substrate specificity not assayed individually for CYP73A11. Confidence medium because substrate inferred from C4H identity. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]
Abstract confirms 'cinnamate 4-hydroxylase activity' in yeast expression after intron removal; substrate not explicitly named in abstract text, inferred from C4H function.

Abstract focuses on expression optimization strategies for monocot P450s (codon usage, N-terminal reengineering) in yeast and tobacco. Wheat C4H identity mentioned contextually but no enzyme assay data or explicit substrate stated in abstract.
Abstract explicitly states: 'Heterologous expression in yeast confirmed that CYP73A19 is the trans-cinnamic acid 4-hydroxylase of chickpea.'

Title only; no abstract available. Title 'Cinnamic acid 4-hydroxylase from Lithospermum erythrorhizon: cDNA cloning and gene expression' indicates C4H function but substrate not confirmed from abstract.
Title only; same paper as CYP73A30 (same DOI). Title indicates C4H function but no abstract to confirm specific substrate from.

Abstract explicitly states: 'Cinnamic acid hydroxylation is a key step' and CYP73A32 expressed in yeast was characterized for C4H mechanism-based inactivation kinetics, confirming cinnamic acid as substrate.
Abstract explicitly states: 'hydroxylates cinnamic acid to form 4-coumaric acid in phenylpropanoid metabolism.' Crystal structure at 1.7 A resolution reported.
Abstract explicitly states: 'An apparent K(m) of 8.9 microM was determined for cinnamate.' Enzymatic activity confirmed in yeast microsomes at 25 C, pH 6.5-7.0.
Abstract explicitly states: 'microsomal preparations from strains expressing both enzymes efficiently converted cinnamic acid to p-coumaric acid with high specific activities.'
Abstract explicitly states: 'The ability of Populus C4H isoforms to convert trans-cinnamate into p-coumaric acid was verified by the examination of yeast recombinant PtreC4H proteins.'

Same paper as CYP73A42v1 (Lu 2006). Abstract verifies 'Populus C4H isoforms' collectively convert trans-cinnamate to p-coumaric acid using yeast recombinant PtreC4H proteins; CYP73A43v1 not individually distinguished in abstract text.

Abstract (Renault 2017) states 'both paralogs can fulfill comparable cinnamate hydroxylase roles both in vitro and in vivo.' CYP73A48 is one of the paralogs studied but not named individually in abstract; substrate inferred from confirmed C4H activity of both paralogs. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]
Title only: 'Molecular cloning and functional characterization of a cinnamate 4-hydroxylase-encoding gene from Camptotheca acuminata.' No abstract available to confirm substrate.

Same paper as CYP73A48 (Renault 2017). The Brachypodium distachyon CYP73 paralogs are used as proxies; abstract confirms 'comparable cinnamate hydroxylase roles both in vitro and in vivo' for both paralogs. CYP73A92 not named individually in abstract.

Same paper as CYP73A92. Same reasoning: both Brachypodium CYP73 paralogs confirmed for cinnamate hydroxylase activity but CYP73A93 not individually named in abstract. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Same paper as CYP73A92/93. Same Brachypodium paralog context; CYP73A94 not individually named in abstract. Three entries (CYP73A92, CYP73A93, CYP73A94) all cite same DOI with same abstract; unclear if all three are distinct proteins from this abstract alone. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Abstract (Marques 2013) characterizes CYP719A23 and CYP719A24 (methylenedioxy bridge formation) in podophyllotoxin pathway. CYP73A107 is not mentioned or characterized in this abstract; no substrate data for CYP73A107 extractable.

Abstract (Abas 2010) is about microsomal membrane isolation methodology from Arabidopsis; completely unrelated to CYP73A260 substrate characterization. No enzymatic or substrate data for CYP73A260 in this abstract.

Abstract (Chen 2011) explicitly identifies PtrC4H1 as one of 'two cinnamic acid 4-hydroxylases (PtrC4H1 and PtrC4H2)' and states 'Cinnamic acid 4-hydroxylation is also mediated by the same protein complexes.' Kinetic data from yeast recombinant proteins reported.
Same paper as PtrC4H1 (Chen 2011). PtrC4H2 explicitly named as one of the cinnamic acid 4-hydroxylases; kinetic efficiency data from yeast recombinant proteins reported.

Abstract explicitly states: 'The favored substrate (trans-cinnamic acid) of all three liverwort C4Hs was the same.' Function field additionally states 3-hydroxycinnamic acid hydroxylation to caffeic acid with lower efficiency; this is consistent with the abstract's confirmation of trans-cinnamic acid as primary substrate.

Same paper as PaC4H (Liu 2017). Abstract explicitly states 'PaC4H and MpC4H1 had a higher level of activity' and confirms trans-cinnamic acid as primary substrate. Secondary substrate (3-hydroxycinnamic acid) from function field, consistent with family activity pattern.

Same paper as PaC4H/MpC4H1. Abstract states all three liverwort C4Hs share trans-cinnamic acid as favored substrate; MpC4H2 had lower activity but same substrate confirmed. Secondary 3-hydroxycinnamic acid substrate not explicitly confirmed for MpC4H2 specifically in abstract (lower activity noted overall).

Title only: 'Characterization and expression patterns of a cinnamate-4-hydroxylase gene involved in lignin biosynthesis and in response to various stresses and hormonal treatments in Ginkgo biloba.' No abstract available.

Abstract (Xia 2017) explicitly states: 'Enzymatic analysis of recombinant proteins expressed in yeast showed that the three enzymes catalyzed the formation of p-coumaric acid (4-hydroxy trans-cinnamic acid) from trans-cinnamic acid.' CsC4Ha is one of the three.
Same paper as CsC4Ha. Abstract confirms all three CsC4H enzymes (CsC4Ha, CsC4Hb, CsC4Hc) convert trans-cinnamic acid to p-coumaric acid in yeast expression.

Same paper as CsC4Ha/CsC4Hb. Abstract confirms all three CsC4H enzymes convert trans-cinnamic acid to p-coumaric acid. CsC4Hc has a larger ORF (1635 bp, 544 aa) compared to CsC4Ha/b (1518 bp, 505 aa).

Abstract (Li 2020) explicitly states: 'Enzymatic analysis of the recombinant proteins expressed in yeast indicated that PbC4H1 and PbC4H3 catalysed the conversion of trans-cinnamic acid to p-coumaric acid.'
Same paper as PbC4H1. Abstract explicitly confirms PbC4H3 catalyzes trans-cinnamic acid to p-coumaric acid. Note: PbC4H2 was NOT confirmed in abstract (only PbC4H1 and PbC4H3 verified enzymatically).

Same abstract as CYP75A1 (Holton 1993). No substrate assay data in abstract. Empty function field. CYP75A3 corresponds to the Hf2 locus; specific substrates require fulltext.

Substrate classes named but individual compound names not specified in abstract. Products not individually named. [QC VERIFIED]

Title only: 'Molecular characterization of the flavonoid biosynthesis of Verbena hybrida and the functional analysis of verbena and Clitoria ternatea F3'5'H genes in transgenic verbena.' No abstract available.
Title only; same paper as CYP75A19v2. F3'5'H function implied by title but no abstract to confirm specific substrates.

substrates: compound 3 (3-hydroxy-N-methylnorcolaurine or equivalent 1-phenethylisoquinoline intermediate in colchicine pathway)
products: compound 4 ([M+H]+=330.1700 Da, mono-hydroxylated at meta position on ring A)
reaction_type: aromatic hydroxylation (meta-hydroxylation on ring A of 1-phenethylisoquinoline alkaloid)
notes: Abstract (Nett 2020) describes 8 genes for N-formyldemecolcine biosynthesis and identifies 'a non-canonical cytochrome P450 that catalyses the ring expansion reaction.' CYP75A109 is not individually named or assigned a substrate in the abstract; specific substrate requires fulltext. reaction_type: oxidation/hydroxylation (iridoid oxidase; multifunctional P450 catalyzing successive hydroxylation/dehydration)
notes: Miettinen et al. 2014 (Nat Commun): reports 'discovery of the last four missing steps of the (seco)iridoid biosynthesis pathway.' CYP76A26 is one of the four new steps, but the abstract does not name the individual substrate for CYP76A26. The pathway context is the seco-iridoid pathway (geraniol → secologanin branch). Fulltext required to assign the specific substrate and reaction. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Miettinen et al. 2014 (Nature Communications). CYP76A26 is the 'missing iridoid oxidase' (IO) in the Catharanthus roseus seco-iridoid pathway. Characterized by functional screening in yeast. Primary substrates: (cis/trans)-iridodial and nepetalactol (preferred). Converts iridodial/nepetalactol → 7-deoxyloganetic acid via successive hydroxylation/dehydration steps (multifunctional). Also converts iridotrial → 7-deoxyloganetic acid efficiently (Kmapp=25 μM, kcat=5.2 s-1). Minor substrates: 8-oxogeraniol (low efficiency, unidentified product); hydroxylates linalool, nerol, citronellol, lavandulol but NOT geraniol. Does NOT convert 7-deoxyloganic acid or 7-deoxyloganetic acid (UGT-dependent step precedes CYP72A224). Essential for monoterpenoid indole alkaloid (MIA) biosynthesis leading to vinblastine/vincristine. Reconstituted full pathway to strictosidine in Nicotiana benthamiana.

Camagna et al. 2020 (Plant Signal Behav): abstract explicitly states 'detoxification of rishitin...mediated by a cytochrome P450 CYP76 family enzyme via hydroxylation of the isopropenyl group resulting in 13-hydroxyrishitin' and 'hydroxylation of solavetivone, lubimin and oxylubimin by the same enzyme.' Also mentions activity on capsidiol and capsidiol 3-acetate (non-potato phytoalexins). Annotated as sesquiterpenoid phytoalexins hydroxylase (SPH). High confidence.

Three papers consistently characterize CYP76B1. Batard 1998 (Plant J): 'microsomes from transformed yeast catalysed NADPH-dependent O-dealkylation of 7-ethoxycoumarin.' Robineau 1998 (Plant Physiol): 'metabolizes...alkoxycoumarins, alkoxyresorufins, and phenylureas...CYP76B1 catalyzes double N-dealkylation of phenylureas.' Didierjean 2002 (Plant Physiol): confirms linuron (single dealkylation), isoproturon, chlortoluron (double dealkylation). All three papers are consistent. High confidence.

Three papers characterize CYP76B6. Collu 2001 (FEBS Lett): 'The encoded CYP76B6 protein has G10H activity when expressed in C. roseus and yeast cells' — geraniol 10-hydroxylase. Hofer 2013 (Metab Eng): 'CYP76B6 emerged as highly specialized multifunctional enzyme catalyzing two sequential oxidation steps leading to formation of 8-oxogeraniol from geraniol.' Hofer 2014 (Plant Physiol) provides additional context for CYP76 family. Substrate is geraniol; primary product is 10-hydroxygeraniol, secondary product 8-oxogeraniol via further oxidation. All papers consistent. High confidence.

Wang et al. 2010 (Biosci Biotechnol Biochem): 'SmG10H was found to have catalytic activity hydroxylating geraniol' in vitro. Overexpression plants showed increased 10-hydroxygeraniol and swertiamarin. 80.2% homology to C. roseus G10H (CYP76B6). High confidence.

Wang et al. 2019 (Plant Physiol): 'CYP76B74 exhibited geranylhydroquinone 3''-hydroxylase activity and produced 3''-hydroxy-geranylhydroquinone.' RNAi in A. euchroma hairy roots confirmed in planta requirement for shikonin biosynthesis. Biochemically characterized with GHQ as substrate. High confidence.

Song et al. 2020 (Phytochemistry): 'CYP76B100 catalyzed the hydroxylation of the geranyl side-chain of GHQ at the C-3'' position to form 3''-hydroxyl geranylhydroquinone (GHQ-3''-OH).' Heterologously expressed in S. cerevisiae and functionally screened with GHQ. High confidence.

This enzyme-catalyzed oxidation to carboxylic acid from GHQ is reported for the first time in this paper. Functionally screened in S. cerevisiae. High confidence.
