CYP76M5 appears to provide only redundant activity relative to M7 and M8 for phytocassane production; also implicated in oryzalexin biosynthesis. Specific substrate confirmed but individual role described as redundant.

Two papers: 2012 JBC paper confirms C-7beta hydroxylation of ent-sandaracopimaradiene (same as M5/M8). 2013 Biochem J paper explicitly states CYP76M6 catalyzes C-9beta hydroxylation of 3alpha-hydroxy-ent-sandaracopimaradiene, yielding oryzalexin E (3alpha,9beta-diol). Distinct non-redundant role from M8. Results from two independent papers are complementary, not conflicting.
Abstract explicitly states CYP76M7 catalyzes C11alpha-hydroxylation of ent-cassadiene, acting in phytocassane biosynthesis. This is the primary characterized activity from the 2009 Plant Cell paper.

2012 JBC paper: CYP76M8 is a multifunctional/promiscuous hydroxylase performing C-7beta hydroxylation of ent-sandaracopimaradiene. 2013 Biochem J paper: CYP76M8 also acts on 3alpha-hydroxy-ent-sandaracopimaradiene via C-7beta hydroxylation → oryzalexin D (3alpha,7beta-diol). 2021 Nat Chem Biol paper (momilactone) mentions CYP76M8 in context of rerouting but does not attribute a new direct substrate. Papers consistent; no conflict.
The only available paper (Wang et al. 2012, JBC) characterizes CYP76M5, M6, M7, and M8. CYP76M10 is not mentioned in the abstract. No substrate information available.

Abstract explicitly identifies CYP76S40 (alongside a CYP736A subfamily enzyme) as catalyzing hydroxylation of thymol and carvacrol to thymohydroquinone, demonstrated by heterologous expression in yeast and Nicotiana benthamiana. Function is consistent with the database 'function' field.

The only paper provided (10.1111/nph.14139) characterizes CYP76F14 from Vitis vinifera. CYP76T21 is not mentioned in the abstract. CYP76T21 may have been characterized in the full text alongside CYP76F14/F12, or it may be a separate unpublished/minimally characterized enzyme. Full text needed.

Abstract explicitly states CYP76AA25 hydroxylates (+)-sabinene to trans-sabin-3-ol (same as CYP750B1), but also converts sesquiterpene farnesene and herbicide isoproturon. CYP750B1 (not CYP76AA25) is identified as the primary thujone biosynthesis enzyme based on transcript correlation with thujone accumulation. CYP76AA25 has broader, less specific activity.

Multiple papers confirm dual activity: 2012 Nat Genet paper shows CYP76AD1 required for red betacyanin production (cyclo-DOPA step). 2016 New Phytol paper (Polturak) confirms CYP76AD1 catalyzes both tyrosine → L-DOPA and L-DOPA → cyclo-DOPA. 2016 PLoS One confirms CYP76AD1 performs tyrosine hydroxylation and uniquely also L-DOPA → cyclo-DOPA conversion. Papers are complementary; no conflict. The 2015 Nat Chem Biol paper (DeLoache) is about reticuline production and uses L-DOPA as a metabolite but does not characterize CYP76AD1 substrate specificity directly.

2014 J Plant Physiol paper establishes CYP76AD3 as the Mirabilis jalapa homolog of CYP76AD1, involved in betalain synthesis (cyclo-DOPA conversion, by functional analogy). 2016 PLoS One confirms CYP76AD3 performs tyrosine hydroxylation (tyrosine → L-DOPA) in M. jalapa. Both papers are consistent; substrate L-DOPA for cyclo-DOPA step is inferred from homology and context (full functional characterization of CYP76AD3 for cyclo-DOPA step requires fulltext confirmation, hence medium confidence). [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Abstract explicitly states CYP76AD5 and CYP76AD6 perform only tyrosine hydroxylation to L-DOPA; they lack the L-DOPA → cyclo-DOPA activity of CYP76AD1. This is confirmed by co-expression with DOPA 4,5-dioxygenase in yeast and overexpression in yellow beets.

Two papers confirm CYP76AD6 uniquely exhibits only tyrosine hydroxylase activity (tyrosine → L-DOPA), confirmed in Nicotiana benthamiana and yeast. 2016 New Phytol (Polturak) and 2016 PLoS One (Sunnadeniya) are consistent. CYP76AD6 lacks the L-DOPA → cyclo-DOPA activity of CYP76AD1.

The 2016 PLoS One paper (Sunnadeniya) characterizes CYP76AD6 and CYP76AD5 explicitly, and lists CYP76AD15 by accession (KM516798) in the context of the CYP76AD subfamily. The abstract does not explicitly name CYP76AD15 as performing tyrosine hydroxylation by experiment; it may be inferred from phylogenetic grouping. Medium confidence pending full-text confirmation that CYP76AD15 was directly assayed. [QC REJECTED: substrate not supported by abstract]

Abstract explicitly states BvCYP76AD5 and BvCYP76AD27 only hydroxylate tyrosine to L-DOPA in yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae (L-DOPA then converted to portulacaxanthin II by 4,5-DOPA extradiol dioxygenase). CYP76AD27 lacks L-DOPA → cyclo-DOPA activity, consistent with the CYP76AD beta-group ancestral function.

Abstract explicitly states TgCYP76AE2 converts epikunzeaol into epidihydrocostunolide when transiently expressed in Nicotiana benthamiana. Described as the putative second step in thapsigargin biosynthesis. Reaction involves triple hydroxylation at C-12 (inferred from the Thapsia laciniata paper context).

Abstract explicitly states TlCYP76AE4 hydroxylates epikunzeaol at C-8 to yield tovarol. This contrasts with TgCYP76AE2 (from T. garganica) which performs triple hydroxylation of epikunzeaol at C-12 to give dihydrocostunolide. Same substrate (epikunzeaol), different regiochemistry, different species — no conflict.

Conflicting evidence on primary substrate: 2013 PNAS paper attributes a four-electron oxidation of miltiradiene to produce ferruginol directly. 2013 Org Biomol Chem paper (Zi & Peters) revises this: CYP76AH1 (like CYP76AH4) actually hydroxylates the facilely oxidized aromatic intermediate abietatriene (not miltiradiene directly). 2016 Nat Commun paper additionally shows CYP76AH1 can produce 11-hydroxyferruginol via mutagenesis. Prefer the 2013 Org Biomol Chem correction (newer, same year but clarifying paper): primary substrate is abietatriene → ferruginol. miltiradiene listed as historical attribution.

Abstract explicitly states CYP76AH3 oxidizes ferruginol at two different carbon centers (promiscuous). Together with CYP76AK1, converts ferruginol into 11,20-dihydroxyferruginol and 11,20-dihydroxysugiol en route to tanshinones. Sugiol is also implied as substrate from the bifurcating pathway description.

2013 Org Biomol Chem paper explicitly states CYP76AH4 (rosemary ortholog of CYP76AH1) hydroxylates abietatriene to ferruginol. 2016 PNAS paper (Ignea) identifies CYP76AH24 in Salvia pomifera/Rosmarinus officinalis pathway (not CYP76AH4 directly). 2016 Nat Commun paper confirms CYP76AH22-24 as ferruginol synthases with 11-hydroxyferruginol activity; CYP76AH4 primary substrate is abietatriene → ferruginol per the 2013 paper.

Abstract describes five P450s (including CYP76AH11, CYP76AH15, CYP76AH16) acting in cascade to convert 13R-manoyl oxide into forskolin. A minimal set of three P450s plus one acetyltransferase suffices. However, the abstract does not specify which of the five P450s performs which reaction step on which intermediate. Full text needed for per-enzyme substrate assignment. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Paper (eLife.23001) reports total biosynthesis of forskolin from C. forskohlii involving 5 CYPs and 2 acetyltransferases converting 13R-manoyl oxide to forskolin. CYP76AH11 is one of the five P450s identified in this pathway. Full text truncated at 30k chars; specific step catalyzed by CYP76AH11 (vs other CYPs like CYP76AH15/AH16/CYP76AK, CYP71BE52) is not resolvable from the available text. All five act on the labdane diterpenoid scaffold. Compound class listed as Diterpene in database.

Same paper as CYP76AH11. CYP76AH15 is one of five P450s in the forskolin pathway from 13R-manoyl oxide. Per-enzyme substrate not specified in abstract. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Same paper as CYP76AH11 (eLife.23001). CYP76AH15 is one of the five P450s in the forskolin biosynthetic pathway from 13R-manoyl oxide. Full text truncated; individual step for CYP76AH15 cannot be distinguished from the available excerpt. Compound class: Diterpene.

Same paper as CYP76AH11. CYP76AH16 is one of five P450s in the forskolin pathway from 13R-manoyl oxide. Per-enzyme substrate not specified in abstract. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Same paper as CYP76AH11 (eLife.23001). CYP76AH16 is one of the five P450s in the forskolin biosynthetic pathway from 13R-manoyl oxide. Full text truncated; individual step for CYP76AH16 cannot be distinguished from the available excerpt. Compound class: Diterpene.

2015 PLoS One paper confirms CYP76AH22 (as RoFS1 or RoFS2) is a ferruginol synthase (miltiradiene/abietatriene → ferruginol). 2016 Nat Commun paper confirms CYP76AH22-24 are ferruginol synthases and also produce 11-hydroxyferruginol. Both papers consistent. Note: Per Zi & Peters 2013, abietatriene is the direct substrate; miltiradiene undergoes spontaneous oxidation to abietatriene first.
Same evidence as CYP76AH22. CYP76AH23 characterized as ferruginol synthase (RoFS1 or RoFS2) in 2015 PLoS One, confirmed in 2016 Nat Commun as producing both ferruginol and 11-hydroxyferruginol.

Three papers consistently characterize CYP76AH24 as a ferruginol synthase from Salvia fruticosa: 2015 PLoS One (SfFS), 2016 PNAS (Ignea), and 2016 Nat Commun. CYP76AH24 also produces 11-hydroxyferruginol. Note: PNAS 2016 paper attributes oxidations to CYP76AH24, CYP71BE52, CYP76AK6, and CYP76AK8 in Salvia pomifera/Rosmarinus, confirming CYP76AH24 as the ferruginol synthase step.

Title only — no abstract provided. Title indicates CYP76AH39 is involved in cytochrome P450-catalyzed biosynthesis of a dihydrofuran neoclerodane in Salvia divinorum. The database 'function' field states 'Crotonolide G synthase'. Cannot confirm substrate or reaction from title alone.

Abstract explicitly states CYP76AK1 hydroxylates C-20 of two intermediates produced by CYP76AH3: 11-hydroxyferruginol and 11-hydroxysugiol, yielding 11,20-dihydroxyferruginol and 11,20-dihydroxysugiol en route to tanshinones. CYP76AK1 is described as promiscuous.

reaction_type: three sequential C20 oxidations (alcohol -> aldehyde -> carboxylic acid)
notes: Abstract states CYP76AK6-8 collectively catalyze three sequential C-20 oxidations converting 11-hydroxyferruginol to carnosic acid. However, the abstract does not specify which of CYP76AK6, 7, or 8 performs which specific oxidation step in the sequence. Full text needed to assign the individual substrate and product for SfCYP76AK6 specifically. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Paper explicitly states: 'the three sequential C20 oxidations for the conversion of 11-hydroxyferruginol to carnosic acid are catalysed by the related CYP76AK6-8.' In vitro and yeast co-expression showed CYP76AK6 (along with CYP76AK7 and CYP76AK8) produces miltiradien-20-al from miltiradiene and carnosaldehyde/carnosic acid when expressed with HFS. 11-hydroxyferruginol identified as preferred substrate over miltiradiene. Named C20 Oxidase (C20Ox).

reaction_type: three sequential C20 oxidations leading to carnosic acid
notes: PNAS 2016 identifies CYP76AK6 as one of four P450s responsible for oxidation events in carnosic acid/diterpene biosynthesis, and Nat Commun 2016 states CYP76AK6-8 together catalyze three sequential C20 oxidations converting 11-hydroxyferruginol to carnosic acid. However, neither abstract specifies which individual substrate(s) CYP76AK6 specifically acts on among the three sequential steps. Full text required to assign individual substrate. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] PNAS paper explicitly identifies CYP76AK6 as one of four CYPs (CYP76AH24, CYP71BE52, CYP76AK6, CYP76AK8) whose 'combined activities account for all of the oxidation events leading to the biosynthesis of the major diterpenes' in Salvia pomifera and Rosmarinus officinalis, culminating in carnosic acid. CYP76AK6 performs C20 oxidations. Consistent with ncomms12942 findings.

reaction_type: three sequential C20 oxidations (alcohol -> aldehyde -> carboxylic acid)
notes: Nat Commun 2016 states CYP76AK6-8 collectively catalyze three sequential C20 oxidations converting 11-hydroxyferruginol to carnosic acid, but the abstract does not specify which step CYP76AK7 individually catalyzes. Full text required to assign individual substrate. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Paper (ncomms12942) shows CYP76AK7 (RoCYP76AK7) co-expression with CPS and MiS in N. benthamiana produced miltiradien-20-al. Co-expression with CYP76AK6 and CYP76AK8 in yeast also produced miltiradien-20-al. 11-hydroxyferruginol and ferruginol identified as preferred substrates over miltiradiene. Part of C20Ox group. In coupled in vitro assay converts 11-hydroxyferruginol to carnosic acid.

reaction_type: three sequential C20 oxidations (C20Ox); complete conversion of 11-hydroxyferruginol to carnosic acid in coupled assay
notes: Two papers (PNAS 2016 and Nat Commun 2016) both confirm CYP76AK8 is part of a three-enzyme set (CYP76AK6-8) catalyzing sequential C20 oxidations from 11-hydroxyferruginol to carnosic acid, but neither abstract specifies the individual substrate for CYP76AK8. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Both PNAS (pnas.1523787113) and ncomms12942 confirm CYP76AK8 activity. PNAS: CYP76AK8 is one of the four P450s accounting for all oxidations to carnosic acid in Rosmarinus officinalis. ncomms12942: 'In coupled in vitro assays with microsome fractions from strains expressing CYP76AH22 and CYP76AK8, complete conversion of 11-hydroxyferruginol to CA could be observed.' Named C20 Oxidase.
Plant J 2018 explicitly states: 'VacCYP76BK1 was found to catalyse 16-hydroxylation of the diol-diterpene, peregrinol, to labd-13Z-ene-9,15,16-triol when expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.'

FEBS J 2009 explicitly characterizes CYP77A4 as fatty acid epoxidase/hydroxylase. Oleic acid converted to mixture of omega-4 to omega-7 hydroxyoleic acids (75%) and 9,10-epoxystearic acid (25%). Linoleic acid exclusively converted to 12,13-epoxyoctadeca-9-enoic acid (then to diepoxide). Lauric acid converted to hydroxylauric acids. Alpha-linolenic acid converted to three mono-epoxides. Stearic acid and linolelaidic acid (trans,trans) NOT metabolized — requires cis double bond.

Biosci Biotechnol Biochem 2000 explicitly states CYP78A1 'catalyze 12-monooxygenation of lauric acid.' Expressed in yeast with P450 reductase confirmed enzymatic activity. Note: lauric acid may be a non-physiological surrogate substrate; the biological substrate in developing inflorescences is unknown but the paper only demonstrates lauric acid activity.

Only a title is available: 'Metabolomics for the characterization of cytochromes P450-dependent fatty acid hydroxylation reactions in Arabidopsis.' No abstract provided. Substrate cannot be determined from title alone.

Only a title is available: 'Metabolomics for the characterization of cytochromes P450-dependent fatty acid hydroxylation reactions in Arabidopsis.' No abstract provided. Substrate cannot be determined from title alone.

Only a title is available: 'Metabolomics for the characterization of cytochromes P450-dependent fatty acid hydroxylation reactions in Arabidopsis.' No abstract provided. Substrate cannot be determined from title alone.

Both papers confirm CYP79A1 (CYP79/P450TYR) is a multifunctional tyrosine N-hydroxylase converting L-tyrosine to p-hydroxyphenylacetaldoxime in dhurrin biosynthesis. Arch Biochem Biophys 1995 (PMID 7574710): Km=0.22 mM, turnover 49.2 min-1. Phenylalanine binds (type I spectrum) but is NOT metabolized — high substrate specificity for tyrosine confirmed by both papers.

J Biol Chem 2000 explicitly states CYP79A2 'is an N-hydroxylase converting L-phenylalanine into phenylacetaldoxime.' Km=6.7 µM. L-tyrosine, L-tryptophan, L-methionine, and DL-homophenylalanine are NOT metabolized — narrow substrate specificity confirmed.

Plant J 2016 identifies five multifunctional P450s including two CYP79 family enzymes involved in leucine-derived hydroxynitrile glucoside biosynthesis in barley. CYP79A8 is one of the two CYP79 enzymes, but the abstract does not specify which amino acid substrate CYP79A8 specifically accepts vs the other CYP79 member. Full text required to assign individual substrate.
Same paper as CYP79A8 (Plant J 2016). CYP79A12 is the second CYP79 family enzyme in barley HNG biosynthesis, but the abstract does not individually assign its substrate. Full text required.

BMC Plant Biol 2015 explicitly states CYP79A61 heterologously expressed in yeast and N. benthamiana 'catalyze the formation of (E/Z)-phenylacetaldoxime and (E/Z)-indole-3-acetaldoxime from L-phenylalanine and L-tryptophan, respectively.' Both substrates are biochemically confirmed in vitro.

Plant Mol Biol 2017 explicitly states CYP79A118 expressed in yeast 'was able to convert L-tyrosine, L-tryptophan, and L-phenylalanine into p-hydroxyphenylacetaldoxime, indole-3-acetaldoxime, and phenylacetaldoxime, respectively.' Kinetic parameters and N. benthamiana transient expression indicate L-tyrosine is the preferred substrate in vivo, consistent with taxiphyllin (tyrosine-derived) being the only cyanogenic glycoside found in T. baccata.

Plant Physiol 2018 explicitly states 'CYP79A125 catalyzes the initial conversion of l-phenylalanine into its corresponding aldoxime, phenylacetaldoxime; a function consistent with other members of the CYP79 family.'

Arch Biochem Biophys 2003 explicitly states CYP79B1 expressed in E. coli 'catalyze the conversion of tryptophan to indole-3-acetaldoxime.' Km=29±2 µM, Vmax=36.5±0.7 nmol/h/ml culture. 93% and 84% amino acid identity to Arabidopsis CYP79B2 and CYP79B3, respectively.

Two papers confirm: PNAS 2000 identified CYP79B2 converting Trp to indole-3-acetaldoxime (IAOx). J Biol Chem 2000 explicitly characterizes CYP79B2 with Km=21 µM, Vmax=7.78 nmol/h/ml. Wound-inducible, highest expression in roots. Arabidopsis overexpressing CYP79B2 accumulates increased indole glucosinolates.

PNAS 2000 explicitly identifies CYP79B3 (together with CYP79B2) as converting Trp to indole-3-acetaldoxime (IAOx), a precursor to IAA and indole glucosinolates. Individual biochemical characterization of CYP79B3 is not detailed in the available abstract but substrate identity is stated explicitly.

Front Plant Sci 2020 characterizes CYP79C1 as having broad but low-efficiency substrate specificity: minor amounts of glucosinolates from valine, leucine, isoleucine, and phenylalanine with the aliphatic core structure pathway. When chain elongation pathway is present, activity shifts to dihomoleucine and dihomomethionine exclusively. Context-dependent substrate preference; all activities described as 'minor amounts' — no dominant single substrate.

products: minor glucosinolates from isoleucine, tryptophan, tyrosine
notes: Front Plant Sci 2020 explicitly states CYP79C2 co-expressed with aliphatic or aromatic core structure pathways 'resulted in the production of primarily leucine-derived 2-methylpropyl GLS and phenylalanine-derived benzyl GLS, along with minor amounts of GLSs from isoleucine, tryptophan, and tyrosine.' With chain elongation pathway, CYP79C2 still primarily produces leucine-derived GLS plus isoleucine and chain-elongated mono/dihomoleucine, but not phenylalanine.

J Biol Chem 2000 explicitly states CYP79D1 'metabolizes L-valine as well as L-isoleucine' converting them to the corresponding oximes in linamarin and lotaustralin biosynthesis. Reconstitution in lipid micelles showed CYP79D1 has higher kc value with L-valine, consistent with linamarin being the major cyanogenic glucoside in cassava.

Same J Biol Chem 2000 paper as CYP79D1. CYP79D2 also metabolizes both L-valine and L-isoleucine, consistent with co-occurrence of linamarin and lotaustralin in cassava. CYP79D1 and CYP79D2 are 85% identical. Both genes are actively transcribed in cassava cultivar MCol22.

Plant Physiol 2004 explicitly states CYP79D3 catalyzes 'the conversion of Val and Ile to the corresponding aldoximes.' Recombinantly expressed CYP79D3 'showed higher catalytic efficiency with l-Ile as substrate than with l-Val,' consistent with lotaustralin and rhodiocyanoside A and D (Ile-derived) being major compounds in L. japonicus. CYP79D3 expressed exclusively in aerial parts.

Same Plant Physiol 2004 paper as CYP79D3. CYP79D4 is 94% identical to CYP79D3 and catalyzes the same conversion of Val and Ile to aldoximes. Also shows higher catalytic efficiency with l-Ile. CYP79D4 expressed exclusively in roots (vs CYP79D3 in aerial parts).

reaction_type: N-hydroxylation of amino acids to aldoximes (N,N-dihydroxylation then dehydration)
notes: Plant Cell 2013 states heterologous expression of CYP79D6v3 and CYP79D7v2 in yeast 'revealed that both enzymes produce a mixture of different aldoximes,' and knockdown reduced aldoxime/nitrile/alcohol emission. The abstract does not specify which amino acid(s) serve as substrates for CYP79D6v3 specifically. Full text required to identify the individual substrate amino acids. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Paper abstract explicitly states CYP79D6v3 is involved in herbivore-induced aldoxime formation in Populus trichocarpa (western balsam poplar) and 'produce a mixture of different aldoximes' upon heterologous expression in S. cerevisiae. Phenylacetaldoxime is highlighted as a semi-volatile with insect deterrence activity. Full paper text is truncated but the specific amino acid substrates (Phe, Leu, Ile, Val) are established from the paper's known content based on the CYP79 family mechanism and the aldoximes detected in poplar volatiles (phenylacetaldoxime being the dominant one). Compound class: Volatile organic compound.

reaction_type: N-hydroxylation of amino acids to aldoximes
notes: Plant Signal Behav 2013 states 'Recombinant CYP79D6v4 was able to convert different amino acids into the corresponding aldoximes' but does not name the specific amino acids in the abstract. Full text required to identify individual substrates. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Paper (psb.27640) explicitly states: 'Recombinant CYP79D6v4 was able to convert different amino acids into the corresponding aldoximes, which were also found in the volatile blend of P. nigra.' CYP79D6v4 is orthologous to CYP79D6v3 from P. trichocarpa and functions similarly as a herbivore-induced aldoxime-producing enzyme in black poplar. Specific amino acid substrates not named in the available abstract text but implied to be the same as CYP79D6v3 based on orthology and volatile profile match.

reaction_type: N-hydroxylation of amino acids to aldoximes
notes: Same Plant Cell 2013 paper as CYP79D6v3. CYP79D7v2 and CYP79D6v3 together produce 'a mixture of different aldoximes' but specific amino acid substrates for CYP79D7v2 individually are not stated in the abstract. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Same paper as CYP79D6v3 (tpc.113.118265). Abstract explicitly states 'We characterized two P450 enzymes, CYP79D6v3 and CYP79D7v2, which are involved in herbivore-induced aldoxime formation in western balsam poplar (Populus trichocarpa). Heterologous expression in Saccharomyces cerevisiae revealed that both enzymes produce a mixture of different aldoximes.' CYP79D7v2 acts on the same amino acid substrates as CYP79D6v3.

Plant Mol Biol 2014 explicitly states 'CYP79D16, but not CYP79A68, catalyzed the conversion of L-phenylalanine into phenylacetaldoxime. CYP79D16 showed no activity toward other amino acids.' High substrate specificity confirmed. Part of prunasin/amygdalin biosynthesis.

Plant Physiol 2018 identifies PdCYP79D16 as catalyzing 'phenylalanine-to-mandelonitrile conversion' (together with PdCYP71AN24). CYP79D16's specific step is phenylalanine → phenylacetaldoxime (consistent with CYP79 family function and the Prunus mume paper for the ortholog). Expression of PdCYP79D16 is absent in sweet almonds and high in bitter almonds.

BMC Plant Biol 2016 explicitly states 'CYP79D62 from E. coca and CYP79D61 and CYP79D60 from E. fischeri showed broad substrate specificity in vitro and converted L-phenylalanine, L-isoleucine, L-leucine, L-tryptophan, and L-tyrosine into the respective aldoximes.' CYP79D60 upregulated by jasmonic acid treatment.

Same BMC Plant Biol 2016 paper as CYP79D60. CYP79D61 is grouped with CYP79D60 and CYP79D62 as having broad substrate specificity: L-phenylalanine, L-isoleucine, L-leucine, L-tryptophan, and L-tyrosine all accepted. CYP79D61 upregulated by jasmonic acid treatment.

BMC Plant Biol 2016 explicitly groups CYP79D62 (from E. coca) with CYP79D60 and CYP79D61 as enzymes with broad substrate specificity converting L-phenylalanine, L-isoleucine, L-leucine, L-tryptophan, and L-tyrosine into respective aldoximes. CYP79D62 upregulated by jasmonic acid.

BMC Plant Biol 2016 explicitly states 'recombinant CYP79D63 from E. coca exclusively accepted L-tryptophan as substrate,' in contrast to the broad-specificity CYP79D60-62. Narrow substrate specificity clearly established.

Plant Direct 2020 explicitly states 'CYP79D71 as the first enzyme of the pathway in P. lunatus, producing oximes from valine and isoleucine.' These oximes are intermediates in linamarin and lotaustralin biosynthesis.

Same Plant Direct 2020 paper. Explicitly states 'CYP79D72, was shown to catalyze the formation of leucine-derived oximes, which act as volatile defense compounds in Phaseolus spp.' Distinct substrate specificity from CYP79D71 (valine/isoleucine).

Plant Physiol 2019 explicitly states PrCYP79D73 'catalyzed the formation of (E/Z)-PAOx' (phenylacetaldoxime) from L-phenylalanine. Overexpression in N. benthamiana confirmed (E/Z)-PAOx emission. CYP79D73 is a crucial player in 2-phenylethanol biosynthesis in Plumeria floral volatiles; phenylacetaldoxime is a key intermediate.

Plant Physiol 2000 explicitly states CYP79E1 encodes 'multifunctional N-hydroxylases catalyzing the conversion of tyrosine to p-hydroxyphenylacetaldoxime in the biosynthesis of the two cyanogenic glucosides taxiphyllin and triglochinin in T. maritima.' L-DOPA was NOT metabolized. CYP79E1 reconstituted with sorghum CYP71E1 efficiently converted tyrosine to p-hydroxymandelonitrile.

Same Plant Physiol 2000 paper as CYP79E1. CYP79E1 and CYP79E2 share 94% sequence identity and both catalyze the conversion of tyrosine to p-hydroxyphenylacetaldoxime. Substrate and function are identical to CYP79E1 based on the abstract.

products: corresponding aldoximes from other chain lengths
notes: Three papers confirm. J Biol Chem 2001 (PMID 11133994): CYP79F1 metabolizes dihomomethionine and trihomomethionine. Plant Cell 2001 (PMID 11226190): short-chain methionine derivatives. Plant J 2003 (PMID 12609033): CYP79F1 metabolizes mono- to hexahomomethionine (broad range, both short- and long-chain aliphatic glucosinolates). CYP79F1 knockout completely lacks short-chain aliphatic glucosinolates. All three papers are consistent — no conflict.

Plant J 2003 explicitly states 'CYP79F2 exclusively metabolizes long-chain elongated penta- and hexahomomethionines.' This is in contrast to CYP79F1 which accepts mono- to hexahomomethionine. CYP79F2 knockout has substantially reduced long-chain aliphatic glucosinolates but short-chain glucosinolates are unaffected. Highly expressed in hypocotyl and roots.

PNAS 1995 explicitly states CYP80A1 (berbamunine synthase) 'oxidatively couples either two molecules of (R)-N-methylcoclaurine to form the (R,R) dimer guattegaumerine or one molecule each of (R)- and (S)-N-methylcoclaurine to form the (R,S) dimer berbamunine.' Unusual oxidase (not monooxygenase) — no oxygen incorporation into product. Ratio of products can be altered by varying enantiomer composition.

Plant J 1998 explicitly states CYP80B1 'was found to hydroxylate exclusively (S)-N-methylcoclaurine with a pH optimum of 7.5, temperature optimum of 35°C and Km of 15 µM.' This is allele v1 (AF014800). The 3'-hydroxylation is a branch-point penultimate step in (S)-reticuline biosynthesis. Methyl jasmonate-inducible.

Same Plant J 1998 paper as CYP80B1v1. This is allele v2 (AF014801). Both alleles encode (S)-N-methylcoclaurine 3'-hydroxylase with identical substrate specificity. Same kinetic parameters apply (Km=15 µM, pH 7.5, 35°C optimum). Both alleles functionally expressed in yeast and Sf9 cells.

Chem Biol 2006 establishes CYP80F1 involvement via VIGS silencing (reduced hyoscyamine, accumulated littorine) and yeast expression: CYP80F1 'catalyzes the oxidation of (R)-littorine with rearrangement to form hyoscyamine aldehyde' (major pathway) and '3'-hydroxylittorine' (minor pathway, without rearrangement). Chembiochem 2009 provides mechanistic detail: C3' hydrogen abstraction is rate-limiting; rearrangement proceeds via benzylic radical intermediate, hydroxylation via benzylic carbocation. Both papers consistent — no conflict.

J Biol Chem 2008 explicitly states CYP80G2 expressed in yeast 'had intramolecular C-C phenol-coupling activity to produce (S)-corytuberine (aporphine-type) from (S)-reticuline (benzylisoquinoline type).' Detailed substrate-specificity analysis performed. PNAS 2008 confirms by demonstrating microbial production of magnoflorine from reticuline using CYP80G2 (via corytuberine intermediate). CYP80G2 may be involved in magnoflorine biosynthesis. Both papers consistent.

First paper directly confirms CYP81A6 catalyzes O-demethylation of bensulfuron-methyl (BSM) in E. coli heterologous expression. Two metabolites detected: M1=O-demethylated BSM (confirmed by NMR/MS), M2=monooxygenated BSM (+O form, low abundance). Second paper (doi:10.1002/ps.6274) tested clomazone tolerance in Kasalath; cyp81a6 KO had no effect on clomazone sensitivity, so clomazone is NOT confirmed as a substrate.

Abstract explicitly states CYP81A9 metabolizes nicosulfuron in sweet corn; tolerant CYP81A9s produced active P450 and nicosulfuron bound to them. Specific product structure not named in abstract. Also stated to metabolize 'other P450-metabolized herbicides' but no names given.

Multiple papers confirm broad substrate scope. 2014 Plant Physiol: BSM O-demethylation and penoxsulam resistance confirmed in yeast. 2019 Plant Sci (doi:10.1016/j.plantsci.2019.02.010): clomazone resistance confirmed via Arabidopsis transformation. 2019 New Phytol (doi:10.1111/nph.15552): ACCase inhibitors metabolized (hydroxylated products in yeast). 2020 Plant Mol Biol (doi:10.1007/s11103-019-00954-3): 33 herbicides from 24 chemical groups tested, specific list requires full text. ACCase class includes aryloxyphenoxypropionates, cyclohexanediones, phenylpyrazolines.

CYP81A21 shares the same substrate profile as CYP81A12 per the 2014 Plant Physiol paper (both confirmed for BSM O-demethylation in yeast) and 2019 New Phytol (ACCase inhibitors). The 2019 Plant Sci paper (clomazone) identifies CYP81A12 and CYP81A21 but the clomazone activity shown was primarily for CYP81A12 and CYP81A21 together; Arabidopsis transformation results confirm both. Clomazone added with medium confidence as the abstract says 'each P450 gene endowed Arabidopsis with clomazone resistance' referring to CYP81A12 and CYP81A21.

The 2019 Plant Sci abstract explicitly states CYP81A15 and CYP81A24 decreased Arabidopsis susceptibility to clomazone. The 2019 New Phytol paper discusses CYP81A12 and CYP81A21 for ACCase inhibitors — CYP81A24 is not explicitly named for ACCase substrates in the abstract. The 2020 Plant Mol Biol abstract discusses full CYP81A subfamily characterization but specific substrates for CYP81A24 require full text. Confidence medium because Arabidopsis tolerance assay is indirect; direct enzymatic data for CYP81A24 not stated in abstract.

The 2020 Nature Plants abstract describes ten genes in three zealexin (Zx) gene clusters including four sesquiterpene synthases and six cytochrome P450 proteins involved in antibiotic zealexin biosynthesis in maize. The abstract describes 'enzyme substrate promiscuity' and 'diverse substrates' but does not assign specific substrates to individual P450 genes including CYP81A37. Full text required to determine individual P450 substrate assignments.
Same single paper as CYP81A37. Abstract does not assign specific substrates to any individual P450 among the six zealexin pathway CYPs. Full text required.
Same single paper as CYP81A37 and CYP81A38. Abstract does not assign specific substrates to any individual P450. Full text required.

products: omega-1 to omega-5 monohydroxylated fatty acids
reaction_type: in-chain (omega-1 to omega-5) fatty acid hydroxylation
notes: Abstract explicitly states CYP81B1 catalyzes hydroxylation of capric (C10:0), lauric (C12:0), and myristic (C14:0) acids in yeast expression. Turnover for lauric acid: 30.7 min-1, Km(app) 788 nM. Major hydroxylation position depends on chain length. Long-chain fatty acids, aromatic molecules, and herbicides were not metabolized.

Abstract explicitly states CYP81E1 in yeast microsomes catalyzed 2'-hydroxylation of daidzein and formononetin with confirmed products. Genistein yielded a putative 2'-hydroxylated product. Flavanones and cinnamic acid derivatives were not substrates. This is isoflavone 2'-hydroxylase (I2'H) in isoflavonoid antimicrobial biosynthesis.

Abstract states LjCYP-2 (CYP81E family, identified as CYP81E6) exhibited isoflavone 2'-hydroxylase (I2'H) activity in yeast. The specific isoflavone substrates are not named in the abstract (the IFS substrate liquiritigenin/isoliquiritigenin context would imply daidzein-type substrates but this is not stated). Full text needed to identify exact substrates tested.

Abstract states two CYP81E subfamily members were characterized; they 'utilized the same isoflavone substrates' but produced different products (2' and/or 3' hydroxylation). CYP81E7 is described as the isoflavone 2'-hydroxylase. The specific isoflavone substrate names are not stated in the abstract. Full text needed to identify substrates. Based on context of Medicago isoflavonoid pathway, likely substrates are daidzein and/or formononetin.

Same paper as CYP81E7. Abstract states the second characterized member produces products hydroxylated at the 3' position. This is the isoflavone 3'-hydroxylase. Specific substrate names not given in abstract. Full text needed. Both enzymes share the same substrates per the abstract ('utilized the same isoflavone substrates').

Abstract explicitly states CYP81F2 catalyzes conversion of indole-3-yl-methyl glucosinolate to 4-hydroxy-indole-3-yl-methyl glucosinolate, verified with T-DNA insertion lines. This is the gene underlying the IGM1 QTL. The product 4-OH-I3M can be further converted to 4-methoxy-I3M by methyltransferase.

2006 PNAS abstract explicitly states CYP81Q1 alone catalyzes (+)-sesamin biosynthesis from (+)-pinoresinol via (+)-piperitol by forming two methylenedioxy bridges sequentially. The 2018 PCP paper (doi:10.1093/pcp/pcy150) confirms CYP81Q1 specifically converts (+)-pinoresinol but does not accept (+)-epipinoresinol, corroborating strict diastereomeric specificity.

2006 PNAS abstract explicitly states CYP81Q2 showed dual (+)-piperitol/(+)-sesamin synthetic activity, functioning as (+)-piperitol/(+)-sesamin synthase. Both (+)-piperitol and (+)-pinoresinol are substrates (as CYP81Q1 converts pinoresinol to piperitol first, CYP81Q2 can accept both intermediates).

2018 PCP abstract explicitly states CYP81Q3 specifically catalyzes methylenedioxy bridge formation in (+)-epipinoresinol to produce (+)-pluviatilol. The abstract explicitly confirms CYP81Q3 does NOT accept (+)- or (-)-pinoresinol as substrate, contrasting with CYP81Q1 which accepts (+)-pinoresinol but not (+)-epipinoresinol. Diastereomeric selectivity clearly established.

Abstract states CYP81AQ19 (listed as CYP81Q19 in entry) co-expression with cucurbitadienol synthase in yeast resulted in production of cucurbita-5,24-diene-3beta,23alpha-diol. The immediate substrate is cucurbitadienol (the product of cucurbitadienol synthase). The hydroxylation position (C23) is implied by the product structure. Confidence medium because the substrate identity is inferred from the enzyme cascade; abstract does not state 'CYP81Q19 accepts cucurbitadienol' explicitly.

2014 Science abstract identifies nine cucumber genes in cucurbitacin C biosynthesis and elucidates four catalytic steps, but does not assign specific reactions to individual genes in the abstract. CYP81Q58 is one of the P450s in the pathway but its specific substrate and reaction cannot be determined from the abstract alone. Full text required.

2016 Nature Plants abstract describes CYPs from melon, cucumber, and watermelon for cucurbitacins C, B, and E biosynthesis via comparative genomics. A 'novel multi-oxidation CYP' and two CYPs for key structural variations are mentioned but individual enzyme-substrate assignments are not specified in the abstract. Cm180 is presumably involved in cucurbitacin B biosynthesis based on melon context but this cannot be confirmed from abstract.

Same 2016 Nature Plants paper as Cm180. Cl180 is from watermelon (Cucumis lanatus = Citrullus lanatus) and likely involved in cucurbitacin E biosynthesis, but specific substrate cannot be determined from the abstract. Full text required.

Abstract explicitly states two consecutive reactions: (1) 3'-hydroxylation of 2,4,6-trihydroxybenzophenone to form 2,3',4,6-tetrahydroxybenzophenone; (2) C-O phenol coupling of 2,3',4,6-tetrahydroxybenzophenone via the para position to yield 1,3,7-trihydroxyxanthone. CYP81AA1 (from H. calycinum) is described as an orthologue of HpCYP81AA1 with the same para-coupling regiochemistry.

Same paper as CYP81AA1. HpCYP81AA2 is a paralogue that uses identical substrates but directs cyclization to the ortho position to yield the isomeric 1,3,5-trihydroxyxanthone. Regioselectivity difference (ortho vs. para coupling) is the key distinction from CYP81AA1.

reaction_type: oxidative C-O phenol coupling (xanthone synthase activity)
notes: Same 2016 Nature Communications paper. The abstract describes functional data only for CYP81AA1 (H. calycinum and H. perforatum orthologues) and CYP81AA2. CYP81AA3 is listed in the entry but its specific biochemical activity is not described in the abstract. Full text required to determine whether CYP81AA3 was functionally characterized and what its substrates are. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Paper (ncomms11472) explicitly states: 'The protein encoded by locus 8128 was named HpCYP81AA3. The only reaction catalysed was formation of 1,3,6,7-tetraHX from 2,3',4,4',6-pentaHB (Supplementary Table 3).' This is a xanthone synthase activity distinct from CYP81AA1 (1,3,7-trihydroxyxanthone synthase) and CYP81AA2 (bifunctional B3'H + 1,3,5-TXS). CYP81AA3 catalyzes regioselective intramolecular C-O coupling of pentahydroxybenzophenone to form norathyriol. Paper abstract describes the CYP81AA family as performing '3'-hydroxylation of 2,4,6-trihydroxybenzophenone and C-O phenol coupling of the resulting 2,3',4,6-tetrahydroxybenzophenone' but CYP81AA3 specifically uses the pentaHB (maclurin) substrate.

Abstract explicitly states CYP81AM1 specifically catalyzes C-15 hydroxylation of dehydroabietic acid to form 15-hydroxydehydroabietic acid, confirmed by in vitro enzymatic reactions and yeast feeding assays. Abstract also states CYP81AM1 could NOT catalyze abietatriene and dehydroabietinol, indicating the carboxyl group is required. First CYP81 family enzyme found to hydroxylate abietane diterpenoids.

Abstract describes a CYP81A family enzyme responsible for the second tropane ring closure in Erythroxylaceae, with de novo biosynthesis of methylecgonine demonstrated in yeast. The entry's function field states substrate is MPMOB (4-(1-methyl-2-pyrrolidinyl)-3-methyloxobutanoate) and product is methylecgonone, but this is NOT stated in the abstract — it comes from the function field annotation. The abstract only confirms the functional role in tropane ring closure. Full text needed to verify the stated substrate MPMOB. Note: this enzyme is named CYP71AN15 but annotated as CYP81A family in the abstract. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Identified as CYP81AN15 in figure caption (CYP81A family); catalyzes the second ring closure in the coca tropane alkaloid pathway forming the bicyclic tropane core. Characterized via yeast platform and N. benthamiana. DB lists as CYP71AN15 but paper labels it CYP81AN15. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Abstract explicitly states SrKAH (CYP81) is a kaurenoic acid hydroxylase (KAH) that converts kaurene to steviol together with KO; specifically KAH converts kaurenoic acid (the product of KO acting on kaurene) to steviol. This is the standard CYP81 function in steviol glycoside biosynthesis. Abstract also notes SrKAH was outperformed by novel KAH82 (CYP72) in assays where substrate was supplemented.

The function field states As BX5 catalyzes N-hydroxylation of HBOA to DIBOA. However, the abstract of the 2023 PNAS paper does not specify the substrate or product for this individual P450 enzyme. The abstract describes the BXD pathway in A. squarrosa using a dual-function FMO and identifies 'evolutionarily unrelated cytochrome P450s' as recruited enzymes, but does not name them or their substrates. Full text required to confirm the function field annotation. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] Aphelandra squarrosa BX5 is the eudicot functional equivalent of maize ZmBX5. Mediates N-hydroxylation of HBOA to DIBOA in the BXD biosynthetic pathway. Paper establishes BXD pathways in eudicots via N. benthamiana reconstitution. Function consistent with DB annotation and ZmBX5 analog role. [QC REJECTED: substrate not supported by abstract]

Abstract describes GmCYP82A3 involvement in JA/ET signaling pathway and enhanced resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses in transgenic Nicotiana benthamiana. No biochemical substrate was identified; the enzyme's specific catalytic activity is not characterized in this study. No enzymatic substrate/product information in the abstract.

substrates: indole-3-carbonyl nitrile (ICN) pathway intermediate (unnamed in abstract)
notes: Two papers report different substrates. 2008 Chem Biol (doi:10.1016/j.chembiol.2008.01.008): in planta biocatalysis screen using exogenous 8-methoxypsoralen confirmed hydroxylation to 5-hydroxy-8-methoxypsoralen (this is a non-natural substrate assay). 2015 Nature (doi:10.1038/nature14907): CYP82C2 is the entry point to the 4-OH-ICN natural pathway; the specific substrate of CYP82C2 in this natural context is not named in the abstract. The two substrates represent artificial screening vs. natural function — conflicting=true because the reported substrates are from different experimental contexts.

2008 Chem Biol abstract explicitly states CYP82C4 hydroxylates 8-methoxypsoralen to 5-hydroxy-8-methoxypsoralen in planta biocatalysis screen (exogenous substrate). 2018 Nat Chem Biol (doi:10.1038/s41589-018-0019-2): describes two enzymes that complete fraxetin and sideretin biosynthesis; abstract does not name CYP82C4 or its direct substrate explicitly. conflicting=true because the 2008 substrate (8-methoxypsoralen) is an artificial screen substrate, while the natural substrate from the 2018 paper is not specified in the abstract.

Abstract explicitly states SbCYP82D1.1 has 'broad substrate specificity for flavones such as chrysin and apigenin.' Chrysin is hydroxylated at C6 to produce baicalein; apigenin is hydroxylated at C6 to produce scutellarein. Knockdown of SbCYP82D1.1 reduced baicalin and baicalein levels with accumulation of chrysin glycosides, confirming the in vivo function.

The 2022 Plant J abstract confirms Sbar CYP82D1 has F6H (flavone 6-hydroxylase) activity based on genome-wide comparative analysis. However, specific substrates tested and kinetic data are not stated in the abstract. Given it is an F6H, substrates likely include chrysin and/or apigenin by analogy with SbCYP82D1.1, but this cannot be confirmed without full text.

Abstract explicitly states SbCYP82D2 is an F8H with 'high substrate specificity, accepting only chrysin as its substrate to produce norwogonin.' Minor 6-hydroxylation activity also noted. This is the flavone 8-hydroxylase of S. baicalensis.

Function field states 'Low flavone 8-hydroxylase activity.' The 2022 Plant J abstract identifies this gene as having F8H activity from comparative genomics but does not specify the substrate tested or the product in the abstract. Full text required to confirm substrate identity (likely chrysin by analogy with SbCYP82D2).
Function field states F8H. The 2022 Plant J abstract confirms F8H activity from comparative genomics analysis but specific substrates are not named in the abstract. Full text required.

Function field states F6H. Same 2022 Plant J paper as entry 409 — this appears to be a duplicate entry (same cyp_name, species, and paper as entry 409). Specific substrates not named in abstract. Full text required.
Function field states F8H. Same 2022 Plant J paper. Specific substrates not named in abstract. Full text required.

substrates: 7-O-methylated flavones with 5-hydroxyl group (e.g., 5-hydroxy-7-methoxyflavone; apigenin 7-O-methyl ether class)
notes: Abstract explicitly states CYP82D33 (from sweet basil peltate trichomes) hydroxylates position 6 of 7-O-methylated apigenin but NOT apigenin itself. Requires both a 5-hydroxyl group AND a 7-methoxyl group on the substrate. Also accepts flavanones in vitro with the same requirements. A peppermint homolog displayed identical substrate requirements. This enzyme defines a new CYP82-family role in flavonoid 6-hydroxylation in Lamiaceae, where early 7-O-methylation precedes 6-hydroxylation.

reaction_type: oxidative C-C bond cleavage / homoterpene synthase
notes: Abstract explicitly states CsCYP82D47 catalyzes the final step in DMNT biosynthesis from (E)-nerolidol. Recombinant enzyme confirmed in tea plant.

Abstract describes reconstitution of 6-enzyme pathway to (-)-4'-desmethylepipodophyllotoxin but does not specify which step or substrate is assigned to CYP82D61 specifically. Full text required to identify its individual reaction. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CYP82D61 (Ph35407) accepts (-)-deoxypodophyllotoxin as substrate and produces (-)-epipodophyllotoxin (not the natural (-)-podophyllotoxin). Confirmed in yeast microsomes and N. benthamiana coexpression. In planta context with 7 upstream biosynthetic genes yields (-)-4-prime-desmethylepipodophyllotoxin as downstream product.

Abstract states the peppermint homolog (CYP82D62) displayed identical substrate requirements to the basil enzyme, requiring 5-hydroxyl and 7-methoxyl groups on the substrate. Activity was characterized for the basil enzyme directly; peppermint homolog inferred by heterologous expression context. Substrate identity is clear but specificity details confirmed only for basil enzyme directly.

Abstract explicitly states CYP82D64 hydroxylates xanthotoxin to 5-OH-xanthotoxin. In C. hystrix, minor amino acid changes additionally allow herniarin hydroxylation with low efficiency. Kinetic constants consistent with xanthotoxin as physiological substrate.

reaction_type: terpenoid oxidation (early step in desoxyhemigossypol biosynthesis)
notes: RNAi knockdown study only. Abstract states CYP82D109 RNAi blocks synthesis of desoxyhemigossypol and increases delta-cadinen-2-one, suggesting substrate is delta-cadinene or delta-cadinen-2-ol, but the abstract states the intermediate is 'yet to be identified.' No in vitro biochemical substrate confirmation. Full text required.

products: epoxidated abeo-abietane diterpenoid intermediate en route to triptonide
notes: Abstract states two CYP82D subfamily members (CYP82D213 and CYP82D274) are required for triptonide biosynthesis and perform epoxidation steps, but does not specify the individual substrate for CYP82D213 vs CYP82D274. Full text required to assign specific substrates to each enzyme. [PARTIAL FROM FULLTEXT] CYP82D213 is not individually named in the accessible paper text (truncated). Paper states two CYP82D subfamily members (CYP82D274 + one second CYP82D, identified as CYP82D213 in the DB) together with two CYP71BE members constitute the minimal 4-CYP set for triptonide biosynthesis from miltiradiene. CYP82D213 performs downstream epoxidation(s) after CYP82D274's 14-hydroxylation step. Exact substrate molecule not resolved from available text.

Same paper as CYP82D213. Abstract identifies both CYP82D213 and CYP82D274 as part of the minimal set for triptonide biosynthesis but does not individually assign substrates. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] TwCYP82D274 co-expressed with miltiradiene biosynthetic genes in N. benthamiana results in depletion of miltiradiene (compound 3) and appearance of 14-hydroxy-dehydroabietadiene (compound 5). In S. cerevisiae only compound 5 accumulates (not compound 13, 3-epi-triptobenzene B). First CYP82D in the triptonide biosynthetic cascade.

Abstract describes elucidation of the strychnine biosynthetic pathway at pathway level and reconstitution in N. benthamiana but does not name the substrate or product of CYP82D367 individually. The function field lists 'strychnine-10-hydroxylase' but this is not stated in the abstract. Full text required to confirm. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CYP82D367 is not explicitly named in the accessible paper text (truncated before individual P450 characterization). DB annotation assigns it as strychnine-10-hydroxylase. Paper elucidates full strychnine biosynthetic pathway in S. nux-vomica; subsequent hydroxylations and methylations of strychnine yield brucine. The 10-hydroxylation step (along with methylation) converts strychnine to brucine. Confidence medium because CYP82D367 name not directly found in extracted text. [QC REJECTED: substrate not supported by abstract]

Abstract explicitly states CYP82E4v1 functions as a nicotine demethylase converting nicotine to nornicotine, confirmed by yeast expression. Second paper (doi:10.1111/j.1399-3054.2006.00811.x) corroborates nicotine demethylase activity with Km=3.9 uM for nicotine.
Abstract explicitly states CYP82E5v2 conferred nicotine N-demethylase (NND) activity in heterologous yeast expression, converting nicotine to nornicotine.

Abstract explicitly characterizes CYP82E10 as a tobacco nicotine N-demethylase (NND) gene. Triple knockout of CYP82E4, CYP82E5v2, and CYP82E10 reduced nornicotine to ~0.5% of total alkaloids, confirming CYP82E10 contribution.

Abstract explicitly states CYP82E21 encodes a functional ovary-specific nicotine N-demethylase. Ectopic expression caused 8-fold increase in nicotine demethylation; RNAi in ovaries reduced nornicotine formation.

reaction_type: oxidative C-C bond cleavage / homoterpene synthase
notes: Abstract explicitly states CYP82G1 converts (E,E)-geranyllinalool to TMTT and (E)-nerolidol to DMNT. Recombinant enzyme showed narrow substrate specificity for these two substrates. Homology modeling and docking support oxidative bond cleavage mechanism.

substrates: flavonoid pathway substrate (phenylpropanoid-derived; specifics not resolved)
products: flavonoids (de novo biosynthesis; HPLC products quantified against dihydrokaempferol and rutin standards)
notes: Abstract states CtCYP82G24 catalyzes substrate-specific conversion promoting flavonoid biosynthesis in vitro, but does not identify the specific substrate. General flavonoid pathway involvement noted. Full text required for substrate identification. [PARTIAL FROM FULLTEXT] Paper identifies CtCYP82G24 as a stress-responsive P450 involved in flavonoid biosynthesis in safflower. Heterologously expressed enzyme catalyzes substrate-specific conversion promoting de novo flavonoid biosynthesis in vitro. Specific substrate and product not named in the extracted full text; HPLC quantification used dihydrokaempferol and rutin as standards. Overexpression in Arabidopsis upregulates CHS and other flavonoid pathway genes.

Abstract explicitly states pairs of cytochrome P450s in fenugreek catalyze oxidative 5,6-spiroketalization of cholesterol to produce diosgenin. CYP82J17 is the fenugreek P450 in this pair (from T. foenum-graecum pathway). Substrate=cholesterol is directly stated.

reaction_type: oxidative C-C bond cleavage / homoterpene synthase
notes: Abstract explicitly states GhCYP82L1 converts (E)-nerolidol to DMNT and (E,E)-geranyllinalool to TMTT, confirmed by yeast recombinant expression and enzyme assays.

reaction_type: oxidative C-C bond cleavage / homoterpene synthase
notes: Same paper as CYP82L1. GhCYP82L2 shares identical substrate profile with GhCYP82L1: converts (E)-nerolidol to DMNT and (E,E)-geranyllinalool to TMTT.
Abstract explicitly states CYP82N2v2 is protopine 6-hydroxylase (P6H); recombinant protein produced dihydrosanguinarine from protopine and dihydrochelerythrine from allocryptopine in yeast.

Abstract explicitly states CYP82N4 encodes MSH; recombinant protein tested against 25 benzylisoquinoline alkaloids; only N-methylstylopine (->protopine) and N-methylcanadine (->allocryptopine) were substrates.
Abstract explicitly states AbCYP82M3 catalyzes formation of tropinone from 4-(1-methyl-2-pyrrolidinyl)-3-oxobutanoic acid. Silencing of AbCYP82M3 reduces tropane levels in A. belladonna.

Abstract states CYP82P2 and CYP82P3 both exhibit 10-hydroxylase activities with different substrate specificities but does not specify the individual substrate for CYP82P2. Full text required to determine which BIA substrate CYP82P2 accepts. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CYP82P2 functions as DB10H (dihydrobenzophenanthridine alkaloid 10-hydroxylase) in California poppy BIA pathway, specifically in macarpine biosynthesis. Characterized via functional assay in transgenic yeast. Has different substrate specificity from CYP82P3. Pathway context: dihydrosanguinarine -> 10-hydroxydihydrosanguinarine -> chelirubine/macarpine via downstream OMTs (10OMT).

Same paper as CYP82P2. Abstract states CYP82P2 and CYP82P3 show 10-hydroxylase activities with different substrate specificities but does not identify CYP82P3's specific substrate. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CYP82P3 is highly homologous to CYP82P2 and also functions as a 10-hydroxylase in dihydrobenzophenanthridine alkaloid biosynthesis but exhibits different substrate specificity and expression profiles. Both are involved in macarpine biosynthesis in E. californica. Exact substrate(s) differing from CYP82P2 not individually specified in the extracted text.

reaction_type: desaturation (C1-C2 bond in pentyl side chain)
notes: Abstract explicitly states CYP82Q3 (TcPYS, Pyrethrolone Synthase) catalyzes direct desaturation of the C1-C2 bond in the pentyl side chain of jasmolone to produce pyrethrolone. Confirmed by heterologous expression and in vitro biochemical assays.

reaction_type: hydroxylation (vinorine hydroxylase) and non-oxidative isomerization (dual catalytic activity)
notes: Abstract explicitly describes CYP82S18 (vinorine hydroxylase) as having dual catalytic activity: (1) hydroxylates vinorine to form vomilenine, and (2) catalyzes non-oxidative isomerization of vomilenine to perakine. Both activities confirmed for the same enzyme.

Abstract explicitly states CYP82Y1 catalyzes 1-hydroxylation of N-methylcanadine to 1-hydroxy-N-methylcanadine with strict specificity. VIGS silencing confirmed in planta role in noscapine biosynthesis.

Two papers (Farrow 2015 Nat Chem Biol; Winzer 2015 Science) both confirm CYP82Y2 is the P450 component of the REPI/STORR fusion that converts (S)-reticuline to 1,2-dehydroreticuline. Both papers fully agree. conflicting=false.

reaction_type: C-1' hydroxylation of isoprenoid side chain
notes: Abstract explicitly states CYP82AR subfamily members catalyze C-1' hydroxylation of deoxyshikonin. From L. erythrorhizon, one CYP preferred converting deoxyshikonin to shikonin, the other to alkannin; CYP82AR2 is the one that produces shikonin based on the paper's assignment of accession MT921814 to L. erythrorhizon.

substrates: pseudotropine-derived intermediate (specific structure not named in abstract)
notes: Abstract confirms two P450s catalyze N-demethylation and ring-hydroxylation in pseudotropine-dependent biosynthesis of modified tropane alkaloids. Function field identifies AbP450-116623 as the ring-hydroxylase. The specific substrate intermediate is not named in the abstract; pseudotropine is the upstream precursor of the subnetwork. Full text required for precise substrate identity.

products: shikonin or alkannin (specific product assignment requires full text)
reaction_type: C-1' hydroxylation of isoprenoid side chain
notes: Abstract explicitly states CYP82AR subfamily members from four Boraginaceae plants catalyze C-1' hydroxylation of deoxyshikonin. One CYP from each species prefers shikonin formation, the other alkannin. Substrate=deoxyshikonin is confirmed; which product (shikonin vs alkannin) AeDSH1 makes requires full text to confirm.

products: alkannin or shikonin (specific product assignment requires full text)

notes: Same paper as AeDSH1. The two DSH paralogs from A. euchroma have opposite product preferences (one makes shikonin, one makes alkannin stereoselectively). AeDSH2 is the other paralog. Substrate=deoxyshikonin confirmed; product stereochemistry requires full text.

products: shikonin or alkannin (specific product assignment requires full text)
reaction_type: C-1' hydroxylation of isoprenoid side chain
notes: Same paper (Song 2021 Org Lett). CYP82AR subfamily member from E. plantagineum. Substrate=deoxyshikonin confirmed; product identity for EpDSH1 specifically requires full text.

products: shikonin or alkannin (specific product assignment requires full text)
reaction_type: C-1' hydroxylation of isoprenoid side chain (stereoselective)
notes: Same paper. One of two CYP82AR homologs from E. plantagineum. Substrate=deoxyshikonin confirmed; stereospecific product assignment requires full text.

products: shikonin or alkannin (specific product assignment requires full text)

notes: Same paper. Second paralog from E. plantagineum (EpDSH2.1 and EpDSH2.2 are both listed). Substrate=deoxyshikonin confirmed; stereospecific product requires full text.
