Also accepts cholesterol (best C27), campestanol, sitosterol (poor C29), and (24R)-ergost-4-en-3-one. Both papers consistent; 2006 provides biochemical details of substrate specificity.

reaction_type: C-22 hydroxylase in brassinosteroid biosynthesis (redundant function with CYP724B1/D11)
notes: Abstract identifies CYP90B2/OsDWARF4 as functioning in C-22 hydroxylation (rate-limiting step of BR biosynthesis) but does not specify the exact substrate(s) biochemically. The abstract focuses on agronomic phenotype of erect leaves and yield. Substrate is presumed to be campesterol and related sterols based on family function, but full text needed for biochemical confirmation.

reaction_type: sterol C-22 hydroxylase; campesterol is the best substrate (brassinosteroid biosynthesis)
notes: Abstract explicitly states CYP90B3 is a C-22 hydroxylase. Campesterol is the best substrate; (24R)-ergost-4-en-3-one also metabolized; cholesterol (C27) and sitosterol (C29) are also converted. Compounds after C-5alpha reduction (campestanol, (24R)-5alpha-ergostan-3-one) are poor substrates.

Abstract states four enzymes (three P450s including CYP90B27v1, and one GABA transaminase) catalyze six steps from cholesterol to verazine. The abstract does not specify which step CYP90B27v1 catalyzes. Full text needed to assign the specific substrate. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CYP90B27 is a cholesterol 22R-hydroxylase that catalyzes the first dedicated step in steroidal alkaloid biosynthesis in V. californicum. It hydroxylates cholesterol at C-22 in the R-configuration to produce 22(R)-hydroxycholesterol. This product feeds into the verazine/cyclopamine biosynthetic pathway. Biochemically characterized via heterologous expression in Sf9 insect cells (Augustin et al., 2015, Plant Journal 82:991-1003, doi:10.1111/tpj.12871). The v1 suffix denotes isoform 1.

reaction_type: multifunctional C-22,16-oxidase of cholesterol; catalyzes both C-22R and C-16 oxidations in diosgenin biosynthesis
notes: 2022 Plant J paper confirms TfCYP90B50 is a single multifunctional enzyme performing both early C22,16-oxidations of cholesterol with strict 22R-stereospecificity. The eudicot fenugreek uses one enzyme where the monocot D. zingiberensis uses two separate P450s. Substrate = cholesterol.

reaction_type: steroid C22 hydroxylation (brassinosteroid-type), minor C16,C22 dihydroxylation
notes: Abstract of Nat Commun 2019 describes pairs of P450s for diosgenin biosynthesis in fenugreek and Paris polyphylla, but the 2022 Plant J follow-up paper attributes both C22,16-oxidations to TfCYP90B50 (single enzyme). The specific role of CYP90B51 is not defined in either abstract. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] TfCYP90B51 is a brassinosteroid C22-hydroxylase homolog from fenugreek. Transient expression in N. benthamiana revealed it primarily catalyzes 22S-hydroxylation of cholesterol (brassinosteroid pathway activity) but also shows minor 16,22-dihydroxylase side-activity that contributed to repeated emergence of diosgenin biosynthesis. The main dihydroxylase activity in T. foenum-graecum is carried by CYP90B50. Christ et al. 2019, Nature Communications 10:3647.

reaction_type: steroid C22 hydroxylation (brassinosteroid-type), minor C16,C22 dihydroxylation
notes: Abstract describes pairs of P450s in Paris polyphylla for diosgenin biosynthesis from cholesterol but does not specify which step CYP90B52 catalyzes. Full text needed. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] PpCYP90B52 from Paris polyphylla is a brassinosteroid C22-hydroxylase. Transient expression studies showed it primarily produces 22S-hydroxycholesterol, with minor amounts of 16,22-dihydroxycholesterol. This minor side-activity parallels TfCYP90B51 and reflects the evolutionary origin of the dedicated dihydroxylase activity (CYP90G4) required for diosgenin biosynthesis. Christ et al. 2019, Nature Communications 10:3647.

reaction_type: cholesterol C-22R-specific hydroxylase in diosgenin biosynthesis
notes: 2022 Plant J abstract explicitly states DzCYP90B71 is specific for 22R-hydroxylation and DzCYP90G6 handles C16-oxidation. Strict 22R-stereospecificity confirmed; 22S-hydroxycholesterol is not a substrate.

reaction_type: brassinosteroid C-23 hydroxylase; redundant function with CYP90D1
notes: Earlier paper (Plant J 2005) proposed CYP90C1 acts in typhasterol to castasterone conversion. The 2006 Plant Cell paper (preferred, newer) revised this: in vitro assays show C-23 hydroxylation of multiple 22-hydroxylated BRs. Preferred substrates are 3-epi-6-deoxocathasterone, (22S,24R)-22-hydroxy-5alpha-ergostan-3-one, and (22S,24R)-22-hydroxyergost-4-en-3-one. Less active on 6-deoxocathasterone. CYP90C1 and CYP90D1 are redundant C-23 hydroxylases.

reaction_type: brassinosteroid C-23 hydroxylase; redundant function with CYP90C1
notes: Same two papers as CYP90C1. The 2005 paper described CYP90D1 as involved in BR pathway (cyp90d1 single mutant no phenotype but double mutant dwarf). The 2006 paper (preferred) shows CYP90D1 is a C-23 hydroxylase with same preferred substrates as CYP90C1. Both are redundant.

reaction_type: steroid C22 oxidation (hydroxyl to ketone); product spontaneously cyclizes to verazine
notes: Same paper as CYP90B27v1. Three P450s (including CYP90G1v3) plus one GABA transaminase catalyze six steps from cholesterol to verazine. The abstract does not specify which step CYP90G1v3 catalyzes. Full text needed. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CYP90G1 (isoform v3) is a 22-hydroxy-26-aminocholesterol 22-oxidase from V. californicum. It catalyzes oxidation of the C22-hydroxyl group of 22(R)-hydroxy-26-aminocholesterol to a ketone, forming 22-keto-26-aminocholesterol. This reactive intermediate spontaneously cyclizes to verazine, a key steroidal alkaloid precursor for cyclopamine and jervine. Biochemically characterized in Sf9 cells (Augustin et al., 2015, Plant Journal 82:991-1003). The v3 suffix denotes isoform 3.

reaction_type: steroid C16 and C22 dihydroxylation (bifunctional oxidase)
notes: Same paper as CYP90B52. Paris polyphylla uses pairs of P450s for diosgenin biosynthesis; the abstract does not specify which step CYP90G4 catalyzes. Full text needed. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] PpCYP90G4 from Paris polyphylla catalyzes the initial 16,22-dihydroxylation of cholesterol, the first committed step in steroidal saponin (diosgenin) biosynthesis. It arose from the ancient CYP90B subfamily (brassinosteroid C22-hydroxylases) by gene duplication and neofunctionalization. The 16,22-dihydroxycholesterol product is subsequently oxidized at C27 and undergoes spontaneous spiroketalization to form diosgenin. Christ et al. 2019, Nature Communications 10:3647.

reaction_type: C-16 hydroxylase acting downstream of CYP90B71 in diosgenin biosynthesis
notes: 2022 Plant J paper explicitly states DzCYP90G6 handles the C16-oxidation in diosgenin biosynthesis, working in tandem with DzCYP90B71 (which does 22R-hydroxylation). The 2020 Plant Commun paper provides broader genomic context but does not specify the substrate in the abstract. The 2022 paper is definitive.

2004 Plant Physiol paper confirms CYP707A1 encodes ABA 8'-hydroxylase via baculovirus-insect cell expression. Both 2004 papers (EMBO J and Plant Physiol) are consistent. Stereospecific for (+)-ABA; does not bind (-)-ABA.

reaction_type: ABA 8'-hydroxylase (ABA catabolism); responsible for rapid ABA decrease during seed imbibition
notes: EMBO J 2004 paper explicitly identifies CYP707A2 as responsible for rapid ABA decrease during seed imbibition. cyp707a2 mutants show hyperdormancy and 6-fold higher ABA. Functional expression in yeast confirmed ABA 8'-hydroxylase activity.

2004 Plant Physiol paper provides most detailed biochemical data: CYP707A3 expressed in insect cells, Km = 1.3 micromolar for (+)-ABA, k_cat = 15 min-1. Does not bind (-)-ABA. Does not have isomerization activity. Product is 8'-hydroxy-ABA which spontaneously isomerizes to phaseic acid.
Both 2004 papers confirm CYP707A4 as an ABA 8'-hydroxylase. The Plant Physiol paper explicitly states CYP707A1 and CYP707A4 also encode ABA 8'-hydroxylase alongside CYP707A3.

reaction_type: ABA 8'-hydroxylase (ABA catabolism); OsABA8ox1, induced by submergence and ethylene
notes: Abstract explicitly states ABA 8'-hydroxylase activity confirmed in yeast microsomes expressing OsABA8ox1 (=CYP707A5). Level of phaseic acid (oxidized ABA form) increased with decreasing ABA under submergence, consistent with enzyme activity.

Abstract states GmCYP707A1a overexpression in atcyp707a2 mutant decreased ABA sensitivity, providing direct biological evidence of ABA 8'-hydroxylase function. This is transgenic complementation evidence, not in vitro biochemical, but the conclusion is unambiguous.

Abstract confirms CaCYP707A-mediated ABA hydroxylation for CaCYP707A1/2/3/4 as a group, driving ABA degradation. No individual in vitro biochemical assay data per isoform shown in abstract. Substrate assignment based on confirmed class function (CYP707A = ABA 8'-hydroxylase) plus abstract statement of 'ABA hydroxylation'. Full text needed to confirm isoform-specific kinetic data.
Same paper and abstract as CACYP707A1. ABA hydroxylation confirmed for the CaCYP707A group collectively. No per-isoform biochemical assay described in abstract.
Same paper and abstract as CACYP707A1. ABA hydroxylation confirmed for the CaCYP707A group collectively. No per-isoform biochemical assay described in abstract.
Same paper and abstract as CACYP707A1. ABA hydroxylation confirmed for the CaCYP707A group collectively. No per-isoform biochemical assay described in abstract.

J Am Chem Soc 2013 abstract explicitly states 'P450 oxidation of thalianol' with heterologous yeast expression and product characterization by HSQC/NMR. First paper (Science 2008) describes gene cluster coexpression only, no biochemical substrate detail. Specific hydroxylation position requires full text.

Abstract explicitly states 'CYP708A15 catalyze the unique C22 hydroxylation of the cucurbitadienol backbone.' Heterologous expression confirmed. Note: database entry cyp_name is CYP70815v2 but abstract nomenclature is CYP708A15.

Abstract explicitly states 'CYP708A16 catalyze the unique C16 hydroxylation of the cucurbitadienol backbone.' Heterologous expression confirmed. Note: database entry cyp_name is CYP70816 but abstract nomenclature is CYP708A16.

reaction_type: C-28 oxidation (three-step: alcohol -> aldehyde -> carboxylic acid)
notes: FEBS Lett 2016 abstract explicitly states CYP716A1 has 'C-28 oxidative activity' consistent with other CYP716A subfamily enzymes. Function field and abstract together confirm activity against alpha-amyrin, beta-amyrin, and lupeol. CYP716A2 in the same paper showed additional 22alpha-hydroxylation, distinguishing it from CYP716A1.

FEBS Lett 2016 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A2 displayed 22alpha-hydroxylation activity against alpha-amyrin that has not been previously reported, which produces the cytotoxic triterpenoid, 22alpha-hydroxy-alpha-amyrin.' Also performs C-28 oxidation per function field. Both activities confirmed by heterologous yeast expression.

Plant Cell 2011: 'CYP716A12 catalyzes the oxidation of beta-amyrin and erythrodiol at the C-28 position, yielding oleanolic acid.' PCP 2011: 'CYP716A12 was characterized as a multifunctional enzyme with beta-amyrin 28-oxidase, alpha-amyrin 28-oxidase and lupeol 28-oxidase activities.' Results consistent across both papers. Metabolomics 2019 paper focuses on CYP72A67/68 and is not primary evidence for CYP716A12 substrates.

Plant Cell 2015 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A14v2 is a P450 belonging to the functionally diverse CYP716 family and catalyzes the oxidation of pentacyclic triterpenes, leading to triterpenes with a carbonyl group at position C-3.' Function field specifies alpha-amyrin and beta-amyrin as substrates and products alpha-amyrone and beta-amyrone. Expressed in S. cerevisiae and N. benthamiana.

PCP 2011 abstract mentions CYP716A15 as a 'homolog of CYP716A12 in grape that is involved in triterpenoid biosynthesis' but does not explicitly state which substrates were tested or which products were formed for CYP716A15 specifically. Full text needed for biochemical confirmation.

Same paper as CYP716A15. Abstract mentions CYP716A17 as a homolog 'involved in triterpenoid biosynthesis' without explicit substrate/product details. Function field states 'Oxidizes beta-amyrin at C-28 to form oleanolic acid' but this is not verifiable from the abstract alone. Full text needed.

Front Plant Sci 2017 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A44 and CYP716A46 exhibited the ordinary C-28 oxidation activity against alpha-amyrin and beta-amyrin to produce ursolic and oleanolic acids, respectively.' In vivo yeast assay confirmed.
Same paper as CYP716A44. Abstract explicitly names CYP716A46 with C-28 oxidation of alpha-amyrin and beta-amyrin. Same evidence and confidence level as CYP716A44.

PCP 2019 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A51 showed triterpenoid C-28 oxidation activity.' Function field specifies lupeol, beta-amyrin, alpha-amyrin as substrates. Loss-of-function analysis in hairy roots showed 'no C-28 oxidized triterpenoids' in cyp716a51 mutant, confirming in planta role.

PCP 2013 abstract explicitly states 'In vitro enzymatic activity assays biochemically confirmed that CYP716A52v2 catalyzed the oxidation of beta-amyrin to produce oleanolic acid' and 'chemical structure of the oleanolic acid product was confirmed using GC/MS.' Transgenic ginseng plants confirmed in planta role in ginsenoside Ro biosynthesis.

Mol Plant 2015 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A75 and CYP87D16, which catalyze the C-28 and C-16alpha oxidations of beta-amyrin, respectively.' Functional analysis performed in M. lanceolata plants and S. cerevisiae.

Plant Sci 2016 abstract states 'functional characterization in yeast led to the identification of CqbAS1, CqCYP716A78 and CqCYP716A79' but does not explicitly state the substrate or product for CYP716A78 in the abstract text. Function field says 'beta-amyrin 28-oxidase' but this cannot be verified from the abstract alone. Full text needed.
Same paper as CYP716A78. Abstract does not explicitly name substrates or products for CYP716A79. Full text needed to confirm.

Plant J 2015 abstract identifies CYP716As in saponin biosynthesis and describes oleanolic acid production from B. vulgaris genes in N. benthamiana, but does not attribute specific substrates to CYP716A80 by name. Function field says 'C-28 oxidase of beta-amyrin and lupeol' but unverifiable from abstract. Full text needed.
Same paper and abstract as CYP716A80. No explicit substrate attribution to CYP716A81 in abstract text. Full text needed.

reaction_type: triterpene C28 three-step oxidation (alcohol -> aldehyde -> carboxylic acid)
notes: Nat Commun 2017 abstract describes characterization of multiple CYP716 enzymes with 'ten hitherto unreported triterpenoid oxidation activities' but does not specify which activity belongs to CYP716A83. Function and biosynthetic_pathway fields are empty. Full text required to determine substrate. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CaCYP716A83 catalyzes the three-step oxidative conversion of alpha-amyrin to ursolic acid and beta-amyrin to oleanolic acid via C28 oxidation (alcohol -> aldehyde -> carboxylic acid). Intermediates erythrodiol and oleanolic aldehyde detected by GC-MS. Characterized by heterologous expression in engineered yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae). Appears functionally more efficient than CYP716A86. Miettinen et al. 2017, Nature Communications 8:14153.

reaction_type: triterpene C28 three-step oxidation (alcohol -> aldehyde -> carboxylic acid)
notes: Same Nat Commun 2017 paper as CYP716A83. Abstract does not specify substrate for CYP716A86. Full text needed. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CaCYP716A86 catalyzes the three-step oxidation at C28 of pentacyclic triterpenes: alpha-amyrin -> ursolic acid, beta-amyrin -> oleanolic acid. Functions similarly to CYP716A83 but with somewhat lower catalytic efficiency in yeast co-expression experiments. Intermediates erythrodiol, ursolic aldehyde detected by GC-MS in co-expression with amyrin synthase. Miettinen et al. 2017, Nature Communications 8:14153.

PCP 2018 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A94 was beta-amyrin 28-oxidase involved in oleanolic acid production from beta-amyrin.' Heterologous yeast expression confirmed; engineered yeast co-expressing KsBAS, CYP716A94 and CYP72A397 produced hederagenin.

Nat Commun 2017 abstract does not specify which activity or substrate corresponds to CYP716A110. Function and biosynthetic_pathway fields are empty. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] AcCYP716A110 from Aquilegia coerulea (Colorado columbine) is a beta-amyrin C28 oxidase producing oleanolic acid via three-step oxidation. GC-MS confirmed erythrodiol and oleanolic acid product peaks consistent with NMR-verified standards. Shows lower catalytic activity compared to Centella asiatica CYP716A83/A86. Characterized in engineered yeast. Miettinen et al. 2017, Nature Communications 8:14153.

Same Nat Commun 2017 paper. Abstract does not specify substrate for CYP716A111. Function and biosynthetic_pathway fields are empty. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] AcCYP716A111 from Aquilegia coerulea catalyzes C16beta hydroxylation of beta-amyrin to produce 16beta-hydroxy-beta-amyrin. Product identity confirmed against NMR-verified 16beta-hydroxy-beta-amyrin standard by GC-MS. This is a distinct regioselectivity from the C28 oxidation catalyzed by other CYP716A members. Characterized in engineered yeast. Miettinen et al. 2017, Nature Communications 8:14153.

Function field explicitly states 'Non-specific reaction of endogenous yeast compound.' This indicates the enzyme showed activity only on an endogenous yeast metabolite in heterologous expression, not a defined plant substrate. Not a characterized plant P450-substrate pair. Nat Commun 2017 abstract provides no further specificity.

Nat Commun 2017 abstract does not specify which activity corresponds to CYP716A140. A second allele (CYP716A140v2) is separately characterized in PCP 2017 (entry 811). For this accession (KU878853), substrate cannot be determined from the abstract. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] PgCYP716A140 (also noted as CYP716A140v2 in some reports) from Platycodon grandiflorus (balloon flower) catalyzes three-step C28 oxidation of beta-amyrin to oleanolic acid. The enzyme produces erythrodiol and oleanolic aldehyde as sequential intermediates. Oleanolic acid then serves as a substrate for downstream CYP716S5-mediated epoxidation in platycoside biosynthesis. Characterized in engineered yeast. Miettinen et al. 2017, Nature Communications 8:14153.

PCP 2017 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A140v2, catalyzed a three-step oxidation reaction at C-28 on beta-amyrin to produce oleanolic acid.' Heterologous expression in engineered yeast producing beta-amyrin confirmed.

PCP 2017 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A141, catalyzed the hydroxylation of beta-amyrin at C-16beta. This reaction is unique among triterpene oxidases isolated to date.' Nat Commun 2017 (second paper) abstract does not specify substrates. PCP 2017 is the definitive characterization paper; no conflict.

Planta 2012 abstract explicitly states 'CrAO was a multifunctional C-28 oxidase converting alpha-amyrin, beta-amyrin and lupeol to ursolic-, oleanolic- and betulinic acids, respectively, via a successive oxidation at the C-28 position.' CrAO corresponds to CYP716A154. Yeast co-expression confirmed.

Appl Microbiol Biotechnol 2019 abstract explicitly states 'RoCYP01 (CYP716A155) was identified...and demonstrated to effectively convert lupeol into BA [betulinic acid].' Expression correlation and yeast metabolic engineering (>1 g/L BA) confirmed. Primary substrate is lupeol; other amyrins may be accepted but not stated in abstract.

New Phytol 2016 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A175 catalyses the C-28 oxidation of alpha-amyrin, beta-amyrin, lupeol and germanicol, producing ursolic acid, oleanolic acid, betulinic acid, and putatively morolic acid.' Morolic acid marked as putative in original paper.

Plant Cell Rep 2017 abstract explicitly states 'Heterologous expression of CYP716A179 in engineered yeast strains confirmed the production of oleanolic acid, ursolic acid, and betulinic acid from beta-amyrin, alpha-amyrin, and lupeol, respectively.' Highest expression in tissue-cultured stolons correlates with oleanolic acid and betulinic acid accumulation.

BMC Biotechnol 2016 abstract explicitly states 'we first isolated a gene encoding a lupeol C-28 oxidase (LO) from Betula platyphylla (designated as BPLO)' and 'BPLO showed a higher activity in BA biosynthesis compared to the previously reported LOs.' BPLO corresponds to CYP716A180 per database function field. Yeast expression confirmed.

Phytochemistry 2017 abstract explicitly states 'beta-amyrin 28-oxidase (CYP716A244)...Oleanolic acid production was confirmed by co-expression of both EsBAS and CYP716A244 in engineered yeast and transgenic tobacco.' Direct biochemical confirmation.

New Phytol 2017 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A252 and CYP716A253 catalyzed sequential three-step oxidation at the C-28 position of alpha-amyrin and beta-amyrin to produce ursolic acid and oleanolic acid, respectively.' Yeast expression and VIGS in sweet basil confirmed.

Same paper as CYP716A252. Abstract explicitly names CYP716A253 with C-28 oxidation of alpha-amyrin and beta-amyrin. Abstract notes 'CYP716A253 was more efficient than CYP716A252 for amyrin C-28 oxidation in yeast.'

BBRC 2018 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A254 encoding a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase from A. flaccida that catalyzes the conversion of the beta-amyrin into oleanolic acid.' Abstract notes 'oxidation of beta-amyrin at the C-18 position' which appears to be a typographical error for C-28 (consistent with all CYP716A subfamily enzymes and the oleanolic acid product). Yeast heterologous expression confirmed.

reaction_type: C-28 oxidation and additional oxidation steps
notes: ACS Synth Biol 2021 abstract states CYP716A262 (CYP091) is involved in biosynthesis of tunicosaponin aglycones gypsogenin and quillaic acid. The platform strain BY-bAS produces beta-amyrin, making it the implied substrate. Abstract does not explicitly name beta-amyrin as the direct substrate in text. Full text needed to confirm exact substrate and reaction steps. Products (gypsogenin, quillaic acid) confirmed at 146.84 and 314.01 mg/L respectively.

Sci Rep 2019 abstract explicitly states 'CYP716A263 oxidized pentacyclic triterpenes at the C-3 position.' Substrates listed are those produced by TkOSC1: taraxasterol, alpha-amyrin, beta-amyrin, lup-19(21)-en-3-ol. Functional characterization in N. benthamiana and S. cerevisiae. This is a C-3 oxidase, not a C-28 oxidase like most CYP716A members.

New Phytol 2019 abstract explicitly states 'Two CYP716 family P450s (CYP716A265, CYP716A266) catalyzed C-28 oxidation of alpha-amyrin, beta-amyrin and lupeol to form ursolic acid, oleanolic acid and betulinic acid, respectively.' Combinatorial expression in S. cerevisiae and N. benthamiana confirmed.
Same paper as CYP716A265. Abstract explicitly names CYP716A266 alongside CYP716A265 with identical substrate/product profile for C-28 oxidation.

BMC Plant Biol 2022 abstract explicitly states 'HaOSC1 and HaCYPi3 encode for lupeol synthase and beta-amyrin oxidase, which produce corresponding products of lupeol and oleanolic acid, respectively.' HaCYPi3 is the beta-amyrin oxidase. Functional verification performed. Note: function field in database says 'beta-amyrin C-28 oxidase' consistent with abstract.

BBRC 2014 abstract explicitly states GbCYP716B 'possessed 9alpha-hydroxylation activity' using in vitro cell-free protein synthesis assays and LC-MS analysis. Activity was demonstrated on taxoid substrate but the exact taxane species tested is not named in the abstract. This enzyme belongs to CYP716B subfamily (diterpene, not triterpene context). Full text needed for exact substrate identity. Confidence medium because substrate class (taxoid) is confirmed but molecular identity not specified in abstract.

Abstract reports ten new CYP716 activities across multiple enzymes from multiple species but does not assign specific substrates to CYP716C11 individually. Full text required to identify which activity belongs to this enzyme. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CaCYP716C11 catalyzes C2alpha hydroxylation of oleanolic acid to maslinic acid and ursolic acid to corosolic acid. In the asiaticoside/madecassoside biosynthesis context in C. asiatica, it acts downstream of CYP716A83/A86 (C28 oxidation) to add the 2alpha-hydroxyl group to the oleanane/ursane scaffold. Also reported to hydroxylate 6beta-hydroxy-oleanolic acid to 6beta-hydroxy-maslinic acid. Miettinen et al. 2017, Nature Communications 8:14153.
Abstract explicitly states: CYP716C55 catalyzed C-2alpha hydroxylation of ursolic acid and oleanolic acid to produce corosolic acid and maslinic acid, respectively.

Abstract explicitly states CYP716E26 exhibited C-6beta hydroxylation activity against beta-amyrin to produce daturadiol. Function field also mentions alpha-amyrin as substrate but abstract only explicitly demonstrates beta-amyrin; alpha-amyrin listed in function hint only.

Same paper as entry 828. Abstract reports ten new CYP716 activities across multiple enzymes but does not assign specific substrates to CYP716E41 individually. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CaCYP716E41 catalyzes C6beta hydroxylation of ursane- and oleanane-type pentacyclic triterpenes. Acting on ursolic acid produces 6beta-hydroxy-ursolic acid; acting on asiatic acid (2alpha-hydroxy-ursolic acid) produces madecassic acid (2alpha,6beta-dihydroxy-ursolic acid), the aglycone of madecassoside. Also converts maslinic acid (2alpha-hydroxy-oleanolic acid) to terminolic acid (6beta-hydroxy-maslinic acid). Key enzyme in madecassoside biosynthetic branch. Miettinen et al. 2017, Nature Communications 8:14153.

Papers describe CYP716A53v2 (protopanaxadiol 6-hydroxylase) and CYP716A47, which are different enzymes from CYP716S1 (accession JX036031). No substrate data is explicitly provided for CYP716S1 in the listed abstracts. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] CYP716S1 (also referred to as CYP716S1v2 in some literature; related to but distinct from CYP716A53v2) from Panax ginseng catalyzes C6alpha hydroxylation of protopanaxadiol (PPD) to produce protopanaxatriol (PPT), key aglycone precursor for PPT-type ginsenosides (e.g., ginsenoside Rg1, Re). The CYP716S subfamily (including S1 from P. ginseng and S5 from P. grandiflorus) are dammarane-type triterpene oxidases. Confidence is medium because the specific DOI 10.1016/j.jgr.2018.02.005 could not be directly retrieved; function is based on published characterization of closely related CYP716S enzymes and cross-referencing with compound class Triterpene in source metadata.

Same Nat Commun 2017 paper as entries 828 and 831. Abstract does not name specific substrates for CYP716S5 individually. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] PgCYP716S5 from Platycodon grandiflorus catalyzes 12,13alpha-epoxidation of the oleanane scaffold. Expression in yeast produced two new peaks: m/z 514 Da identified as 12,13alpha-epoxy-beta-amyrin (vs beta-amyrin m/z 498 Da) and m/z 586 Da corresponding to 12,13alpha-epoxy-oleanolic acid. This epoxidation is a key step in the biosynthesis of platycodon-type triterpenoid saponins (platycosides). The CYP716S subfamily (S1 from P. ginseng, S5 from P. grandiflorus) represents a distinct functional clade of dammarane/oleanane epoxidases. Miettinen et al. 2017, Nature Communications 8:14153.
Papers describe CYP716A47 (dammarenediol-II 12-hydroxylase) and CYP716A53v2, not CYP716U1 (accession JN604536). No substrate data explicitly provided for CYP716U1 in the listed abstracts.

Abstract explicitly states CYP716Y1 catalyzes C-16alpha hydroxylation of oleanane- and ursane-type triterpenes. Specific named substrates include oleanolic acid and ursolic acid (implied by combinatorial biosynthesis context), but class-level substrates are explicitly stated.

2005 PNAS abstract explicitly lists all seven substrates and their Km values. Multisubstrate, multifunctional enzyme. 2016 Plant Physiol provides additional context on clade III activity. Products include abietic acid and related diterpene resin acids.

species: Pinus sitchensis, Pinus contorta, Pinus banksiana
notes: Abstract explicitly states clade I enzymes (CYP720B2 and CYP720B12) convert 13-hydroxy-8(14)-abietene, which is a recently discovered unstable diterpene synthase product. Unlike clade III, not active with diterpene olefins. Products include abietic acid, neoabietic acid, levopimaric acid, palustric acid via an alternative route.

products: diterpene resin acids (DRAs) including abietic acid, neoabietic acid, levopimaric acid, palustric acid, pimaric acid, isopimaric acid, sandaracopimaric acid
notes: 2011 Plant Physiol abstract explicitly states CYP720B4 was active with 24 different diterpenoid substrates, most active in forming dehydroabietic acid. Clade III enzyme. Second paper (2016) provides comparative context with clade I.

species: Pinus sitchensis, Pinus contorta, Pinus banksiana
notes: Abstract explicitly names CYP720B12 as a clade I enzyme alongside CYP720B2, both converting 13-hydroxy-8(14)-abietene. Not active with diterpene olefins. Same substrate and product profile as CYP720B2 (entry 837).

Abstract describes five multifunctional CYP450s in ginkgolide biosynthesis collectively, including C-C bond cleavage and NIH shift reactions, but does not specify which individual reactions CYP720B31 catalyzes. Full text required to assign substrates to this specific enzyme.

Abstract identifies the DSD gene (a CYP) responsible for 5-deoxystrigol formation in Lotus japonicus. The substrate is described as downstream of MAX1, but the specific substrate (carlactonoic acid) is not explicitly named in this abstract. The 2019 Sci Adv paper (VuCYP722C, entry 842) names carlactonoic acid explicitly for the related cowpea enzyme. Full text needed to confirm substrate identity for this Lotus enzyme.
Abstract explicitly states: 'direct conversion of carlactonoic acid to orobanchol without passing through 4-deoxyorobanchol is catalyzed by the recombinant enzyme.' Confirmed by knockout in tomato.

Same paper as VuCYP722C (entry 842). SlCYP722C knockout in tomato resulted in undetectable orobanchol in root exudates, confirming the enzyme catalyzes carlactonoic acid to orobanchol conversion in Solanum lycopersicum.

Abstract explicitly states: 'GaCYP722C...catalyze the conversion of CLA to 5DS but not to 4-deoxyorobanchol.' Product is 5-deoxystrigol (5DS), not orobanchol, distinguishing it from cowpea/tomato CYP722C homologs. C-ring configuration differs.

Abstract states CYP724B1/D11 functions in C-22 hydroxylation, the rate-limiting step of brassinosteroid biosynthesis, but does not explicitly name the substrate. Full text or the companion CYP724B2 paper (tomato) implies campesterol as likely substrate; however, the specific substrate for CYP724B1 is not stated in this abstract.

Abstract explicitly states: 'CYP724B2 catalyzes C-22 hydroxylation of campesterol...campesterol was the best substrate.' Also metabolizes (24R)-ergost-4-en-3-one (to some extent), cholesterol, and sitosterol. (24R)-5alpha-ergostan-3-one and campestanol are poor substrates.

Abstract explicitly states the enzyme transforms taxadienyl acetate to the 10beta-hydroxy derivative. Described as taxane 10beta-hydroxylase. This is the second cytochrome P450 step in Taxol biosynthesis.

Abstract explicitly states: 'taxane 13 alpha-hydroxylase...taxa-4(20),11(12)-dien-5alpha-ol and its acetate ester as test substrates.' Substrate specificity studies indicate multiple biosynthetic routes to Taxol may exist.

Abstract explicitly states: enzyme transforms 5alpha-acetoxy-10beta-ol taxadiene to 5alpha-acetoxy-10beta,14beta-dihydroxy taxadiene, but not the 5alpha,13alpha-diol. 14beta-hydroxylase is a side-route enzyme, not on the main Taxol pathway.

reaction_type: multistep: C-5alpha hydroxylation and/or epoxidation leading to oxetane ring formation
notes: Four papers with partially conflicting characterizations. 2004 Chem Biol: 5alpha-hydroxylase producing taxa-4(20),11(12)-dien-5alpha-ol. 2008 JBC: same substrate but product is 5(12)-oxa-3(11)-cyclotaxane (OCT) in a yeast system and Nicotiana system. 2017 Protein Expr Purif: confirms taxadiene->taxadiene-5alpha-ol. 2024 JACS (newest): CYP725A4 catalyzes two successive epoxidations leading to oxetane ring formation; both taxadiene isomers are substrates. The 2024 paper resolves earlier discrepancy, positioning CYP725A4 as an epoxidase/oxetane synthase prior to C5 acetylation. Preferred interpretation: 2024 JACS.
Abstract explicitly states taxoid 7beta-hydroxylase screened using taxusin as surrogate substrate, producing 7beta-hydroxytaxusin. Operates in the central portion of the Taxol biosynthetic pathway.

Abstract explicitly states taxoid 2alpha-hydroxylase using taxusin as surrogate substrate (Km ~10.5 uM). Both 2alpha- and 7beta-hydroxylases can convert each other's pentaol tetraacetate products to the common hexaol tetraacetate.

Abstract explicitly states: 'Recombinant SbCYP728B35 catalyzed the conversion of 5DS to sorgomol in vitro.' The C-8bS configuration in the C-ring is essential for the reaction. Overexpression in Lotus japonicus hairy roots also confirmed sorgomol production.

products: carboxylic acid derivative of dehydroabietic acid
notes: Abstract explicitly states CYP728B70 'can catalyze oxidation of a methyl to the acid moiety of dehydroabietic acid in triptolide biosynthesis.' Product is the carboxylic acid derivative of dehydroabietic acid; precise intermediate identity in triptolide pathway requires full text for confirmation.

reaction_type: oxidative C-C bond cleavage generating tert-butyl moiety; multi-step oxidation with carbon skeleton rearrangement (NIH shift)
notes: Same Nat Commun 2022 paper as entry 840. Five CYP450s collectively generate tert-butyl group and one lactone ring in ginkgolide biosynthesis, but individual substrate for CYP7005C1 is not specified in the abstract. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] GbCYP7005C1 co-expressed with GbLPS (levopimaradiene synthase) in N. benthamiana and S. cerevisiae. Accumulates compound 7 (ginkgosinoic acid A, C20H30O2) and compound 8 (C20H30O1) from levopimaradiene. Figure 2g shows proposed reaction scheme. The reaction involves scarless C-C bond cleavage that generates the tert-butyl moiety present in all ginkgolides. GbCYP7005C1 and GbCYP7005C3 share >98% amino acid identity and show identical catalytic activities. Substrate is levopimaradiene, the main diterpene hydrocarbon product of GbLPS from GGPP.

reaction_type: oxidative C-C bond cleavage generating tert-butyl moiety; multi-step oxidation with carbon skeleton rearrangement (NIH shift)
notes: Same Nat Commun 2022 paper as entries 840 and 855. Individual substrate for CYP7005C3 not specified in the abstract. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] GbCYP7005C3 shares >98% amino acid identity with GbCYP7005C1 and has identical catalytic activity. Both enzymes produce the same compounds (ginkgosinoic acid A and compound 8) from levopimaradiene when co-expressed with GbLPS in N. benthamiana or yeast. Same paper and reaction as CYP7005C1. Compounds 8 and 9 confirmed as side-product and intermediate respectively by feeding studies.

1998 BBRC: omega-hydroxylation of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids C12-C18. 2008 J Exp Bot: key enzyme for root suberin monomer biosynthesis, omega-hydroxyacids with chain length <C20. 2007 PNAS: associated with suberin biosynthesis when co-expressed with GPAT5. Chain range C12-C18 explicitly stated.

2004 EMBO J: CYP86A2 catalyzes fatty acid oxidation; cutin content reduced 70% in att1/cyp86a2 mutant. 2007 Proteins: lauric acid and oleic acid used as test substrates in binding assays; CYP86A2 shows highest high-spin state proportion of the five CYP86A members. Specific substrate chain range not fully characterized in these abstracts; C12 and C18:1 are explicitly tested substrates.

2005 Plant Physiol: expression characterization, no specific substrate assay in abstract. 2007 Proteins: 'all CYP86A proteins are capable of hydroxylating oleic acid' including CYP86A4; lauric acid and oleic acid are the two test substrates. Activity level not individually quantified vs CYP86A2 in abstract; confidence is medium.

2007 Proteins: CYP86A7 and CYP86A8 produce 'extremely low proportions of high spin state heme even with the most effectively bound fatty acids.' 'All CYP86A proteins are capable of hydroxylating oleic acid' — but very low activity implied. Substrates lauric acid and oleic acid tested; functional activity at low level only.

2001 PNAS (LCR/CYP86A8): 'catalyzes omega-hydroxylation of fatty acids ranging from C12 to C18:1...palmitic and oleic acids were efficient substrates for LCR.' 9,10-epoxystearate was not metabolized. Implicated in cutin biosynthesis and prevention of postgenital organ fusions.

reaction_type: very long chain fatty acid omega-hydroxylation
notes: Abstract explicitly states cyp86B1 mutants show 'strong reduction' in C22- and C24-hydroxyacids and alpha,omega-dicarboxylic acids. Presumed precursors C22 and C24 fatty acids accumulated. CYP86B1 is a very long chain fatty acid hydroxylase for suberin polyester monomer biosynthesis.

Title only: 'Metabolomics for the characterization of cytochromes P450-dependent fatty acid hydroxylation reactions in Arabidopsis.' No abstract available. Cannot determine specific substrates or products from title alone.

1998 Biochem J: omega-hydroxylation of C10-C16 saturated and C18:1/2/3 unsaturated fatty acids; lauric, myristic, and linolenic acids highest turnover. 1999 Biochem J: also hydroxylates 9,10-epoxystearic acid and 9,10-dihydroxystearic acid; enantioselective for (9R,10S)-epoxide.

products: hydroxylauric acid (omega, omega-1, omega-2 depending on chain length)
reaction_type: medium chain fatty acid hydroxylation (chain-length-dependent regioselectivity)
notes: 1999 BBRC: myristic acid is best substrate (Km 4.0 uM, turnover 80 min-1); lauric and palmitic at 10-fold lower rate; C18 fatty acids not oxidized. Regiospecificity varies with chain length. 2001 Arch Biochem Biophys: mutagenesis study with lauric acid confirms regioselectivity shift. Not a strict omega-hydroxylase (chain-length-dependent).

products: 12-hydroxyl-JA-Phe and/or 12-aldehyde-JA-Phe (specific product not fully disambiguated in abstract)
notes: 2015 Phytochem: 'CYP94B1, CYP94B3 and CYP94C1 differentially oxidized JA-Phe to 12-hydroxyl, 12-aldehyde and 12-carboxyl derivatives.' Substrate (JA-Phe) is explicit, but exact product(s) for CYP94B1 specifically are not disambiguated in the abstract. Full text required for product assignment. Only paper listed for this entry.

2011 PCP and 2011 PNAS: CYP94B3 encodes JA-Ile 12-hydroxylase; converts JA-Ile to 12OH-JA-Ile. 2012 JBC: CYP94B3 efficiently performs initial hydroxylation of JA-Ile to 12OH-JA-Ile, with little conversion to 12COOH-JA-Ile. 2015 Phytochem: also hydroxylates JA-Phe to 12OH-JA-Phe. Consistent across all four papers.

reaction_type: fatty acid in-chain hydroxylation; jasmonate conjugate C-12 carboxylation
notes: 2007 FEBS J: lauric acid omega-hydroxylase also forming diacid (dodecadioic acid); also acts on C12-C18 fatty acids. 2012 JBC: CYP94C1 preferentially produces 12COOH-JA-Ile from JA-Ile (two-step oxidation). 2015 Phytochem: also carboxylates JA-Phe. Multisubstrate enzyme with both fatty acid and jasmonate conjugate activities.

Abstract states Paris polyphylla and fenugreek each recruited 'pairs of cytochromes P450 that catalyze oxidative 5,6-spiroketalization of cholesterol to produce diosgenin.' Cholesterol is the overall starting material, but which specific oxidation step CYP94D108 catalyzes (vs. its partner CYP94D109) is not stated in the abstract. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] PpCYP94D108 acts as a functional partner with PpCYP90G4 to catalyze conversion of cholesterol to diosgenin (a spirostanol-type saponin aglycone) in N. benthamiana and RH6829 yeast. The CYP pair together catalyzes oxidative 5,6-spiroketalization. Neither enzyme alone is sufficient for diosgenin production. The text does not resolve which of the two oxidation steps each partner performs individually (text truncated before mechanistic details). PpCYP94D109 and PpCYP72A616 are identified as alternative functional partners to CYP90G4.

Same paper as CYP94D108 (entry 869). Paired CYP450 in diosgenin biosynthesis from cholesterol. Individual substrate/step not specified for CYP94D109 in the abstract. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] PpCYP94D109 is identified alongside PpCYP94D108 as an alternative functional partner for PpCYP90G4 in diosgenin biosynthesis from cholesterol. The pair PpCYP90G4 + PpCYP94D109 is sufficient to reconstitute diosgenin production in N. benthamiana (pooled screen POOL 3 results). CYP94D108 yielded more diosgenin than CYP94D109 in the N. benthamiana assay. The specific oxidation step catalyzed individually by CYP94D109 is not resolved in the truncated text. Same paper as CYP94D108.

2022 Plant J abstract characterizes DzCYP90B71 (22R-hydroxylation of cholesterol) and DzCYP90G6 (C16-oxidation) — neither is CYP94D143. CYP94D143 is not mentioned by name in the abstract. Its assignment to diosgenin biosynthesis pathway comes from the biosynthetic_pathway field, not from this abstract. Full text or a different paper required.

2021 Plant Commun abstract describes diosgenin biosynthesis pathway evolution in D. zingiberensis and yeast engineering, but does not name CYP94D144 specifically. Cannot determine the individual enzyme's substrate from this abstract. Full text required.

substrates: cholesterol (pathway-level; direct substrate of CYP94N1v2 step not resolved)
reaction_type: steroid alkaloid biosynthesis (cholesterol to verazine pathway)
notes: Abstract states three CYP450s together produce verazine from cholesterol (first six steps of cyclopamine biosynthesis), but individual substrate/step assignments for CYP94N1v2 specifically are not stated. Full text required to determine which of the six steps this enzyme catalyzes. [PARTIAL FROM FULLTEXT] CYP94N1v2 is a splice variant of CYP94N1, one of three cytochrome P450s (along with CYP90B27 and CYP72A208) plus a gamma-aminobutyrate transaminase that catalyze the first six steps from cholesterol to verazine (a predicted precursor to cyclopamine). Functional refactoring in Sf9 insect cells confirmed the four-enzyme set produces verazine from cholesterol. The paper text is truncated at 30,000 chars and does not reach the section where individual enzyme substrate assignments are described. The specific direct substrate of CYP94N1v2 within the pathway cannot be confirmed from available text. Based on published literature, CYP94N1 is likely involved in a C-22 or C-26 oxidation step.

Abstract characterizes DzCYP90B71 and DzCYP90G6 for diosgenin biosynthesis in D. zingiberensis; CYP94N8 is not mentioned anywhere in the abstract. No substrate information for CYP94N8 can be extracted. Full text required.

reaction_type: midchain alkane hydroxylation; secondary alcohol oxidation to ketone
notes: Abstract explicitly identifies CYP96A15 (MAH1) as midchain alkane hydroxylase (MAH1). Mutant lacks secondary alcohols and ketones; ectopic overexpression in leaves produces midchain secondary alcohols and ketones matching stem wax. Catalyzes hydroxylation of alkanes to secondary alcohols and possibly a second hydroxylation to ketones. Predominant chain lengths are C29 based on stem wax composition.

reaction_type: terminal (omega) hydroxylation of alkanes to primary alcohols
notes: Abstract explicitly states WSL5/CYP96B5 catalyzes terminal hydroxylation of alkanes yielding odd-numbered primary alcohols. wsl5 mutant shows increased C23-C33 alkanes and reduced C29 primary alcohol. Heterologous expression in Arabidopsis and tobacco confirms C29 primary alcohol production. Reaction direction is alkane to primary alcohol.

reaction_type: oxidative para-para' C-C phenol coupling; minor para-ortho' phenol coupling
notes: Abstract explicitly states CYP96T1 catalyzes para-para' C-C phenol coupling of 4'-O-methylnorbelladine to form (10bR,4aS)-noroxomaritidine and (10bS,4aR)-noroxomaritidine. Also produces para-ortho' product N-demethylnarwedine as <1% of total product. First phenol-coupling P450 characterized from a monocot.

Abstract explicitly states heterologous expression in yeast demonstrated CYP704B1 catalyzes omega-hydroxylation of long-chain fatty acids. Specific chain lengths not stated in the abstract (described only as 'long-chain fatty acids'). Full text required for precise substrate chain length specification. Role in sporopollenin biosynthesis for pollen exine development.

reaction_type: beta-ring hydroxylation at C-3 of carotenoids
notes: PNAS 2006 paper (Kim & DellaPenna) explicitly states CYP97A3 (LUT5 locus) has major in vivo activity toward beta-ring of alpha-carotene and minor activity on beta-rings of beta-carotene. Proposed pathway: alpha-carotene -> (CYP97A3, beta-ring hydroxylation) -> zeinoxanthin -> (CYP97C1, epsilon-ring hydroxylation) -> lutein. Confirmed by 2009 Plant Cell Physiol paper (Kim et al.) showing CYP97 duplicates have different in vivo substrates.

reaction_type: carotene beta-ring hydroxylation (C-3 hydroxylation of beta-ring)
notes: 2007 Arch Biochem Biophys paper describes use of E. coli system to test CYP97 family activity in rice but does not explicitly state the substrate specificity or products of CYP97A4 in the abstract. 2012 Plant Physiol paper discusses synergistic interactions of CYP97A and CYP97C class enzymes in lutein formation but does not name CYP97A4 specifically. Full text required to confirm substrate. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] OsCYP97A4 belongs to the CYP97 clan A family, characterized as carotene beta-ring hydroxylases. Quinlan et al. 2007 (Arch Biochem Biophys) amplified cDNAs from Oryza sativa and used E. coli functional complementation to characterize CYP97 members. Quinlan et al. 2012 (Plant Physiol) confirmed that CYP97A and CYP97C are functionally non-interchangeable: CYP97A enzymes hydroxylate beta-rings; formation of lutein (alpha-carotene pathway) requires coexpression of CYP97A (beta-ring) + CYP97C (epsilon-ring). Full body text of Arch Biochem 2007 paper not available in manuscript (PDF-only access for body text, only metadata returned). Confidence based on abstract-level evidence + family-level biochemistry.

reaction_type: beta-ring hydroxylation at C-3 of alpha-carotene
notes: Abstract states CYP97A29 and CYP97C11 encode the P450 carotenoid beta- and epsilon-hydroxylases of tomato respectively (A29=beta-hydroxylase, C11=epsilon-hydroxylase). Functional characterization was done in planta via transgenic plants. The abstract states the enzymes model lutein synthesis in tomato but does not explicitly name the substrate molecule; substrate identity (alpha-carotene, beta-ring) is inferred from the characterization as the beta-ring hydroxylase in the lutein pathway. Full text recommended for explicit biochemical confirmation.

Abstract states overexpression data indicate a role for CYP97B3 in carotenoid biosynthesis but does not specify its substrate or product. The study includes CYP97B3 as a candidate with overexpression analysis alongside CYP97A3 and CYP97C1, but the abstract does not state what carotenoid CYP97B3 acts on. Full text required for substrate identification.

products: zeinoxanthin (from alpha-carotene, beta-ring hydroxylation also possible)
reaction_type: epsilon-ring hydroxylation at C-3 of alpha-carotene/zeinoxanthin; also exhibits beta-ring hydroxylation activity
notes: PNAS 2004 paper (Tian et al.) explicitly identifies LUT1 as CYP97C1 encoding a cytochrome P450 epsilon-ring carotenoid hydroxylase. 2009 Plant Cell Physiol paper (Kim et al.) confirms CYP97C1 can efficiently hydroxylate both beta- and epsilon-rings of alpha-carotene (triple mutant with only CYP97C1 retains 74% of wild-type lutein). Proposed pathway: alpha-carotene -> (CYP97A3) -> zeinoxanthin -> (CYP97C1, epsilon-ring) -> lutein. Multiple consistent papers, no conflicts.

reaction_type: carotene epsilon-ring hydroxylation (C-3 hydroxylation of epsilon-ring in alpha-carotene pathway)
notes: Same two papers as CYP97A4 (entry 880). Abstract of 2007 Arch Biochem Biophys paper describes E. coli complementation system for rice CYP97 family but does not specify CYP97C2 substrate. 2012 Plant Physiol paper discusses CYP97A and CYP97C class interactions without naming CYP97C2 specifically. Full text required. [UPDATED FROM FULLTEXT] OsCYP97C2 belongs to the CYP97 clan C family, characterized as carotene epsilon-ring hydroxylases. Plant Physiol 2012 abstract explicitly states: formation of lutein requires coexpression of CYP97A and CYP97C enzymes; CYP97C hydroxylates the epsilon-ring of alpha-carotene. CYP97C2 interacts physically with CYP97A enzymes in vivo (bimolecular fluorescence complementation) and in vitro (pull-down assay). The sequential action is: alpha-carotene -> CYP97A4 (beta-ring) -> zeinoxanthin -> CYP97C2 (epsilon-ring) -> lutein. Full body text of Arch Biochem 2007 paper not available (manuscript metadata only). Confidence based on abstract + family-level biochemistry from Plant Physiol 2012.

reaction_type: epsilon-ring hydroxylation at C-3 of alpha-carotene/zeinoxanthin
notes: Abstract characterizes CYP97A29 and CYP97C11 as the P450 carotenoid beta- and epsilon-hydroxylases of tomato (C11=epsilon-hydroxylase). Substrate identity inferred from characterization as epsilon-ring hydroxylase in lutein biosynthesis pathway, consistent with the characterized Arabidopsis CYP97C1 (LUT1) homolog. Full text recommended for explicit biochemical substrate confirmation. [QC: plausible but not directly verified from abstract]

Abstract explicitly states simultaneous incubation of CYP97C27 and CPR I with substrate geranylgeraniol (GGOH) and NADPH led to formation of product plaunotol. CYP97C27 catalyzes the last hydroxylation step of the plaunotol biosynthetic pathway. Expressed as recombinant protein in E. coli (pET32a/BL21(DE3)) for in vitro characterization.

Abstract explicitly states CitCYP97C functioned as an epsilon-ring hydroxylase to produce lutein using zeinoxanthin as a substrate. When CitHYb (beta-ring hydroxylase) was co-expressed with CitCYP97C, alpha-carotene was hydroxylated sequentially on beta-ring then epsilon-ring to produce lutein. Substrate explicitly named in abstract.

Abstract explicitly states CYP710A1 exhibits C-22 desaturase activity with beta-sitosterol to produce stigmasterol (Km=1.0 microM, kcat=0.53 min-1). Overexpression in Arabidopsis increased stigmasterol levels 6- to 32-fold. Expressed in baculovirus/insect cell system for biochemical characterization.

Abstract explicitly states CYP710A2 was able to produce brassicasterol from 24-epi-campesterol and stigmasterol from beta-sitosterol. T-DNA insertion mutant and overexpression analyses confirmed both substrate specificities in planta.

Abstract explicitly states CYP710A11 from tomato (Lycopersicon esculentum) exhibits C-22 desaturase activity with beta-sitosterol to produce stigmasterol (Km=3.7 microM, kcat=10 min-1). Expressed in baculovirus/insect cell system.

Abstract explicitly states recombinant CYP710A13 (baculovirus/insect cell system) exhibited C22-desaturase activity with beta-sitosterol to produce stigmasterol. Km=1.0 +/- 0.043 microM. Abstract explicitly states campesterol and 24-epi-campesterol were NOT accepted as substrates.

Abstract explicitly states recombinant CYP710A14 exhibited C22-desaturase activity with beta-sitosterol to produce stigmasterol. Km=2.1 +/- 0.17 microM. Campesterol and 24-epi-campesterol not accepted. Overexpression in Arabidopsis T87 cells increased stigmasterol 20- to 72-fold. Same substrate as CYP710A13.

reaction_type: consecutive oxidations at C-19 of carlactone (methyl group to carboxylic acid)
notes: PNAS 2014 paper explicitly states MAX1 (CYP711A1) catalyzed consecutive oxidations at C-19 of carlactone to convert the C-19 methyl group into carboxylic acid, producing carlactonoic acid (CLA). Recombinant MAX1 expressed in yeast microsomes; CL incubated directly with protein. 2018 New Phytol paper confirms A1-type classification (CL->CLA is conserved). Endogenous CLA and its methyl ester (MeCLA) also identified in Arabidopsis plants by LC-MS/MS.

reaction_type: oxidative B-C lactone ring closure on carlactone
notes: Nat Chem Biol 2014 paper describes two rice MAX1 homologs: one converts CL to ent-2'-epi-5-deoxystrigol, another converts ent-2'-epi-5-deoxystrigol to orobanchol. Based on database annotation (CYP711A2 vs CYP711A3 differentiation), CYP711A2 is assigned as the CL-to-ent-2'-epi-5-deoxystrigol enzyme. The abstract does not individually name CYP711A2 by accession, so confidence is medium. The 2018 New Phytol paper classifies rice as A2-type (CL -> 4DO via CLA).

reaction_type: hydroxylation/structural conversion of ent-2'-epi-5-deoxystrigol to orobanchol
notes: Nat Chem Biol 2014 paper describes one rice MAX1 homolog converting ent-2'-epi-5-deoxystrigol to orobanchol. Based on database annotation, CYP711A3 is assigned as this second rice MAX1 enzyme. Abstract does not individually name CYP711A3 by accession, so confidence is medium. The 2018 New Phytol paper groups rice as A2-type (CL -> 4DO via CLA); CL may also be a substrate. Full text recommended for accession-level substrate assignment.

Only the 2018 New Phytol paper is available. The abstract classifies MAX1 homologs into three types but does not individually assign CYP711A6 to a specific type or state its substrate. CYP711A6 is likely CL-oxidizing but full text required for explicit substrate determination.

Only the 2018 New Phytol paper. Abstract notes CLA was detected in poplar root exudates, consistent with a MAX1 A1-type function (CL -> CLA), but CYP711A7 is not individually named in the abstract. Full text required to confirm substrate and product for this specific enzyme.

Only the 2018 New Phytol paper. Same situation as CYP711A7 (entry 897). Populus has two MAX1 homologs (CYP711A7 and CYP711A8) but the abstract does not distinguish their individual activities. Full text required.

reaction_type: consecutive oxidations of carlactone: CL -> CLA -> 18-OH-CLA
notes: Abstract explicitly states recombinant LjMAX1 (CYP711A9) expressed in yeast microsomes converted carlactone (CL) to 18-hydroxycarlactonoic acid (18-OH-CLA) via carlactonoic acid (CLA). Identity of 18-OH-CLA confirmed by LC-MS/MS comparison with synthetic standard. (11R)-CL detected as endogenous compound in L. japonicus root.

Only the 2018 New Phytol paper. Maize is listed as one of the species tested but CYP711A13 is not individually named in the abstract. Abstract only states that the conversion of CL to CLA is a common reaction and provides a 3-type classification. Full text required to confirm which maize MAX1 homologs and their specific activities.

2021 New Phytol paper (Yoda et al.) explicitly states CYP711A cytochrome P450 enzymes (SbMAX1 proteins) in sorghum produce 18-OH-CLA from carlactone. SbCYP711A13 is one of the SbMAX1 proteins. The abstract attributes the production of 18-OH-CLA collectively to 'SbMAX1 proteins' without individually distinguishing SbCYP711A13 from SbCYP711A19 and SbCYP711A31, hence medium confidence.

Only the 2018 New Phytol paper. Selaginella is one of the species tested; CLA was detected in Selaginella root exudates suggesting A1-type activity. However CYP711A17v1 is not individually named or assigned in the abstract. Full text required.

Same 2018 New Phytol paper as CYP711A17v1. Selaginella has at least two MAX1 homologs (v1 and v3) and the abstract does not differentiate their activities. Full text required to assign substrate to CYP711A17v3 specifically.
Only the 2018 New Phytol paper. Maize has multiple MAX1 homologs (CYP711A13, CYP711A18, CYP711A19). The abstract does not individually name or assign activities to CYP711A18. Full text required.

2021 New Phytol paper (Yoda et al.) attributes 18-OH-CLA production to SbMAX1 proteins collectively; SbCYP711A18 is one of the SbMAX1 enzymes. The 2021 Plant Physiol paper (Wakabayashi et al.) in this entry is actually about SbCYP728B35 (sorgomol synthase) and does not provide substrate data for SbCYP711A18. Confidence medium due to collective attribution.

Only the 2018 New Phytol paper. Same situation as CYP711A13 (entry 900) and CYP711A18 (entry 904). Maize is tested as a species but CYP711A19 is not individually named or assigned a substrate in the abstract. Full text required.

2021 New Phytol paper (Yoda et al.) attributes 18-OH-CLA production to SbMAX1 proteins (CYP711A enzymes) collectively in sorghum. SbCYP711A19 is one of these SbMAX1 proteins. Individual enzyme activities not differentiated in abstract. Confidence medium.

reaction_type: oxidation of carlactone to carlactonoic acid
notes: 2018 New Phytol (15131) paper explicitly states SlMAX1 catalyzes the formation of carlactonoic acid from carlactone (demonstrated by transient expression of SlMAX1 with SlD27, SlCCD7, SlCCD8 in Nicotiana benthamiana). Slmax1 TILLING mutants show strongly reduced production of orobanchol, solanacol and didehydro-orobanchol isomers. The 2018 New Phytol (15055) paper groups tomato as A1-type (CL -> CLA), consistent. No conflicts between papers.

2021 New Phytol paper (Yoda et al.) states SbMAX1 proteins (CYP711A enzymes) in sorghum produce 18-OH-CLA from carlactone. CYP711A31 is one of the sorghum SbMAX1 proteins alongside SbCYP711A13 and SbCYP711A19. Individual activities not differentiated in abstract. Confidence medium.
